children.text: na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ nāpy ahetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Not from themselves, nor from another, nor from both, nor without a cause—

children.text: utpannā jātu vidyante bhāvāḥ kva cana ke cana // MMK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: do any entities whatsoever ever arise anywhere. (MMK 1.1)

children.text: catvāraḥ pratyayā hetur ārambaṇam anantaram /
children.translated_text: There are four <s>pratyayas</s> (conditions): the cause (<s>hetu</s>), the object-support (<s>ārambaṇa</s>), the immediately preceding,

children.text: tathaivādhipateyaṃ ca pratyayo nāsti pañcamaḥ // MMK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: and likewise the dominant (<s>adhipateya</s>); there is no fifth condition. (MMK 1.2)

children.text: na hi svabhāvo bhāvānāṃ pratyayādiṣu vidyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) of entities is not found in conditions and so forth;

children.text: avidyamāne svabhāve parabhāvo na vidyate // MMK_1.3 //
children.translated_text: when <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) is not found, <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature) is not found either. (MMK 1.3)

children.text: kriyā na pratyayavatī nāpratyayavatī kriyā /
children.translated_text: Action does not possess conditions, nor is action devoid of conditions;

children.text: pratyayā nākriyāvantaḥ kriyāvantaś ca santy uta // MMK_1.4 //
children.translated_text: conditions are not without action—and are conditions then possessed of action? (MMK 1.4)

children.text: utpadyate pratītyemān itīme pratyayāḥ kila /
children.translated_text: It arises dependent on these—thus these are said to be conditions;

children.text: yāvan notpadyata ime tāvan nāpratyayāḥ katham // MMK_1.5 //
children.translated_text: as long as it does not arise, why are these then not non-conditions? (MMK 1.5)

children.text: naivāsato naiva sataḥ pratyayo 'rthasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: A condition is fitting neither for a non-existent nor for an existent object;

children.text: asataḥ pratyayaḥ kasya sataś ca pratyayena kim // MMK_1.6 //
children.translated_text: of what non-existent thing is there a condition? And what need has an existent thing of a condition? (MMK 1.6)

children.text: na san nāsan na sad asan dharmo nirvartate yadā /
children.translated_text: When a <s>dharma</s> (entity) is produced neither as existent, nor as non-existent, nor as both existent and non-existent,

children.text: kathaṃ nirvartako hetur evaṃ sati hi yujyate // MMK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: how can a producing cause be appropriate in such a case? (MMK 1.7)

children.text: anārambaṇa evāyaṃ san dharma upadiśyate /
children.translated_text: It is taught that an existent <s>dharma</s> is without an object-support;

children.text: athānārambaṇe dharme kuta ārambaṇaṃ punaḥ // MMK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: and if the <s>dharma</s> is without an object-support, whence again an object-support? (MMK 1.8)

children.text: anutpanneṣu dharmeṣu nirodho nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: When <s>dharmas</s> have not arisen, cessation is not tenable;

children.text: nānantaram ato yuktaṃ niruddhe pratyayaś ca kaḥ // MMK_1.9 //
children.translated_text: therefore the immediately-preceding is not fitting; and what condition is there for what has ceased? (MMK 1.9)

children.text: bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvānāṃ na sattā vidyate yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the existence of entities devoid of <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) is not found,

children.text: satīdam asmin bhavatīty etan naivopapadyate // MMK_1.10 //
children.translated_text: the statement 'this being, that arises' is simply not tenable. (MMK 1.10)

children.text: na ca vyastasamasteṣu pratyayeṣvasti tat phalam /
children.translated_text: That result does not exist in the conditions, whether taken separately or collectively;

children.text: pratyayebhyaḥ kathaṃ tac ca bhaven na pratyayeṣu yat // MMK_1.11 //
children.translated_text: how can that which does not exist in the conditions come from the conditions? (MMK 1.11)

children.text: athāsad api tat tebhyaḥ pratyayebhyaḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: And if that [result], though non-existent [in them], proceeds from those conditions,

children.text: apratyayebhyo 'pi kasmān nābhipravartate phalam // MMK_1.12 //
children.translated_text: why does a result not also proceed from non-conditions? (MMK 1.12)

children.text: phalaṃ ca pratyayamayaṃ pratyayāścāsvayaṃmayāḥ /
children.translated_text: The result is made of conditions, yet the conditions are not made of themselves;

children.text: phalamasvamayebhyo yattatpratyayamayaṃ katham // MMK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: how can a result that comes from things not made of themselves be made of conditions? (MMK 1.13)

children.text: tasmān na pratyayamayaṃ nāpratyayamayaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, no result is found that is made of conditions or not made of conditions;

children.text: saṃvidyate phalābhāvāt pratyayāpratyayāḥ kutaḥ // MMK_1.14 //
children.translated_text: since there is no result, whence conditions or non-conditions? (MMK 1.14)

children.text: gataṃ na gamyate tāvad agataṃ naiva gamyate /
children.translated_text: What has been gone to is not being gone to; what has not yet been gone to is likewise not being gone to;

children.text: gatāgatavinirmuktaṃ gamyamānaṃ na gamyate // MMK_2.1 //
children.translated_text: apart from the gone-to and the not-yet-gone-to, the being-gone-to is not being gone to. (MMK 2.1)

children.text: ceṣṭā yatra gatis tatra gamyamāne ca sā yataḥ /
children.translated_text: Where there is movement, there is going; and since that [movement] is in the being-gone-to,

children.text: na gate nāgate ceṣṭā gamyamāne gatis tataḥ // MMK_2.2 //
children.translated_text: not in the gone-to nor in the not-yet-gone-to—the going is therefore in the being-gone-to. (MMK 2.2)

children.text: gamyamānasya gamanaṃ kathaṃ nāmopapatsyate /
children.translated_text: How can the going of what is being gone to be tenable,

children.text: gamyamānaṃ vigamanaṃ yadā naivopapadyate // MMK_2.3 //
children.translated_text: when the being-gone-to without going is itself not tenable? (MMK 2.3)

children.text: gamyamānasya gamanaṃ yasya tasya prasajyate /
children.translated_text: For one who holds that going belongs to what is being gone to, it follows

children.text: ṛte gater gamyamānaṃ gamyamānaṃ hi gamyate // MMK_2.4 //
children.translated_text: that there is a being-gone-to without going—for the being-gone-to is being gone to [by going]. (MMK 2.4)

children.text: gamyamānasya gamane prasaktaṃ gamanadvayam /
children.translated_text: If going belongs to the being-gone-to, a twofold going follows:

children.text: yena tad gamyamānaṃ ca yac cātra gamanaṃ punaḥ // MMK_2.5 //
children.translated_text: that by which it becomes the being-gone-to, and that which is again the going in it. (MMK 2.5)

children.text: dvau gantārau prasajyete prasakte gamanadvaye /
children.translated_text: Two goers would follow if a twofold going were entailed,

children.text: gantāraṃ hi tiraskṛtya gamanaṃ nopapadyate // MMK_2.6 //
children.translated_text: for without a goer, going is not tenable. (MMK 2.6)

children.text: gantāraṃ cet tiraskṛtya gamanaṃ nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: If, without a goer, going is not tenable,

children.text: gamane 'sati gantātha kuta eva bhaviṣyati // MMK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: then in the absence of going, whence indeed will a goer come? (MMK 2.7)

children.text: gantā na gacchati tāvad agantā naiva gacchati /
children.translated_text: A goer does not go; a non-goer likewise does not go;

children.text: anyo gantur agantuś ca kas tṛtīyo 'tha gacchati // MMK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: what third one, other than a goer and a non-goer, goes? (MMK 2.8)

children.text: gantā tāvad gacchatīti katham evopapatsyate /
children.translated_text: How can it be tenable that a goer goes,

children.text: gamanena vinā gantā yadā naivopapadyate // MMK_2.9 //
children.translated_text: when without going a goer is not tenable at all? (MMK 2.9)

children.text: pakṣo gantā gacchatīti yasya tasya prasajyate /
children.translated_text: For one who holds the thesis that 'the goer goes,' it follows

children.text: gamanena vinā gantā gantur gamanam icchataḥ // MMK_2.10 //
children.translated_text: that there is a goer without going—for he who desires going for the goer [presupposes a goer]. (MMK 2.10)

children.text: gamane dve prasajyete gantā yadyuta gacchati /
children.translated_text: Two goings would follow if the goer goes:

children.text: ganteti cājyate yena gantā san yac ca gacchati // MMK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: that by which he is designated as 'goer,' and that which, being a goer, he goes. (MMK 2.11)

children.text: gate nārabhyate gantuṃ gantuṃ nārabhyate 'gate /
children.translated_text: Going is not begun in the gone-to; going is not begun in the not-yet-gone-to;

children.text: nārabhyate gamyamāne gantum ārabhyate kuha // MMK_2.12 //
children.translated_text: going is not begun in the being-gone-to—where then is going begun? (MMK 2.12)

children.text: na pūrvaṃ gamanārambhād gamyamānaṃ na vā gatam /
children.translated_text: Prior to the beginning of going, there is neither the being-gone-to nor the gone-to

children.text: yatrārabhyeta gamanam agate gamanaṃ kutaḥ // MMK_2.13 //
children.translated_text: where going could begin; how is there going in the not-yet-gone-to? (MMK 2.13)

children.text: gataṃ kiṃ gamyamānaṃ kim agataṃ kiṃ vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: What gone-to? What being-gone-to? What not-yet-gone-to is imagined,

children.text: adṛśyamāna ārambhe gamanasyaiva sarvathā // MMK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: when the beginning of going is in no way perceived? (MMK 2.14)

children.text: gantā na tiṣṭhati tāvad agantā naiva tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: A goer does not stand still; a non-goer likewise does not stand still;

children.text: anyo gantur agantuś ca kas tṛtīyo 'tha tiṣṭhati // MMK_2.15 //
children.translated_text: what third one, other than a goer and a non-goer, stands still? (MMK 2.15)

children.text: gantā tāvat tiṣṭhatīti katham evopapatsyate /
children.translated_text: How can it be tenable that a goer stands still,

children.text: gamanena vinā gantā yadā naivopapadyate // MMK_2.16 //
children.translated_text: when without going a goer is not tenable at all? (MMK 2.16)

children.text: na tiṣṭhati gamyamānān na gatān nāgatād api /
children.translated_text: One does not come to rest from the being-gone-to, nor from the gone-to, nor from the not-yet-gone-to;

children.text: gamanaṃ saṃpravṛttiś ca nivṛttiś ca gateḥ samā // MMK_2.17 //
children.translated_text: going, arising, and cessation are the same as going [in their analysis]. (MMK 2.17)

children.text: yad eva gamanaṃ gantā sa eveti na yujyate /
children.translated_text: That the going itself is the goer—this is not tenable;

children.text: anya eva punar gantā gater iti na yujyate // MMK_2.18 //
children.translated_text: that the goer is something other than the going—this too is not tenable. (MMK 2.18)

children.text: yad eva gamanaṃ gantā sa eva hi bhaved yadi /
children.translated_text: If the going itself were the goer,

children.text: ekībhāvaḥ prasajyeta kartuḥ karmaṇa eva ca // MMK_2.19 //
children.translated_text: then the identity of agent and action would follow. (MMK 2.19)

children.text: anya eva punar gantā gater yadi vikalpyate /
children.translated_text: If, on the other hand, the goer is imagined as other than the going,

children.text: gamanaṃ syād ṛte gantur gantā syād gamanād ṛte // MMK_2.20 //
children.translated_text: there would be going without a goer, and a goer without going. (MMK 2.20)

children.text: ekībhāvena vā siddhir nānābhāvena vā yayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Neither through identity nor through difference

children.text: na vidyate tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate // MMK_2.21 //
children.translated_text: is the establishment of these two found; how then can it be found at all? (MMK 2.21)

children.text: gatyā yayājyate gantā gatiṃ tāṃ sa na gacchati /
children.translated_text: The going by which the goer is designated—that going he does not go;

children.text: yasmān na gatipūrvo 'sti kaścid kiṃcid dhi gacchati // MMK_2.22 //
children.translated_text: for no one exists prior to going, and yet someone goes something. (MMK 2.22)

children.text: gatyā yayājyate gantā tato 'nyāṃ sa na gacchati /
children.translated_text: The going by which the goer is designated—he does not go a going other than that;

children.text: gatī dve nopapadyete yasmād eke tu gantari // MMK_2.23 //
children.translated_text: for two goings are not tenable in a single goer. (MMK 2.23)

children.text: sadbhūto gamanaṃ gantā triprakāraṃ na gacchati /
children.translated_text: A really existing goer does not perform a threefold going;

children.text: nāsadbhūto 'pi gamanaṃ triprakāraṃ sa gacchati // MMK_2.24 //
children.translated_text: nor does a non-existing goer perform a threefold going. (MMK 2.24)

children.text: gamanaṃ sadasadbhūtaḥ triprakāraṃ na gacchati /
children.translated_text: A goer who both exists and does not exist does not perform a threefold going;

children.text: tasmād gatiś ca gantā ca gantavyaṃ ca na vidyate // MMK_2.25 //
children.translated_text: therefore, going, the goer, and that which is to be gone to—none of these exist. (MMK 2.25)

children.text: darśanaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasanaṃ sparśanaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the mind—

children.text: indriyāṇi ṣaḍ eteṣāṃ draṣṭavyādīni gocaraḥ // MMK_3.1 //
children.translated_text: these are the six <s>indriyas</s> (sense faculties); the visible and the rest are their domains. (MMK 3.1)

children.text: svam ātmānaṃ darśanaṃ hi tat tam eva na paśyati /
children.translated_text: Seeing does not see itself,

children.text: na paśyati yad ātmānaṃ kathaṃ drakṣyati tat parān // MMK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: its own self; that which does not see itself, how can it see others? (MMK 3.2)

children.text: na paryāpto 'gnidṛṣṭānto darśanasya prasiddhaye /
children.translated_text: The analogy of fire is not sufficient to establish [the nature of] seeing;

children.text: sadarśanaḥ sa pratyukto gamyamānagatāgataiḥ // MMK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: that, together with seeing, has been refuted by the [analysis of] the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to. (MMK 3.3)

children.text: nāpaśyamānaṃ bhavati yadā kiṃ cana darśanam /
children.translated_text: When seeing does not see anything at all,

children.text: darśanaṃ paśyatīty evaṃ katham etat tu yujyate // MMK_3.4 //
children.translated_text: how is it tenable to say 'seeing sees'? (MMK 3.4)

children.text: paśyati darśanaṃ naiva naiva paśyaty adarśanam /
children.translated_text: Seeing does not see, and non-seeing likewise does not see;

children.text: vyākhyāto darśanenaiva draṣṭā cāpy avagamyatām // MMK_3.5 //
children.translated_text: through seeing alone the seer too should be understood as explained. (MMK 3.5)

children.text: draṣṭā nāsty atiraskṛtya tiraskṛtya ca darśanam /
children.translated_text: Without setting aside or without not setting aside seeing, there is no seer;

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ caiva draṣṭary asati te kutaḥ // MMK_3.6 //
children.translated_text: if there is no seer, whence the visible and seeing? (MMK 3.6)

children.text: pratītya mātāpitarau yathoktaḥ putrasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the birth of a son is said to be dependent on mother and father,

children.text: cakṣūrūpe pratītyaivamukto vijñānasaṃbhavaḥ // MMK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: so too the arising of consciousness is said to be dependent on the eye and form. (MMK 3.7)

children.text: draṣṭavyadarśanābhāvād vijñānādicatuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: Due to the non-existence of the visible and of seeing, the fourfold group beginning with consciousness

children.text: nāstīty upādānādīni bhaviṣyanti punaḥ katham // MMK_3.8 //
children.translated_text: does not exist; how then will appropriation and the rest come to be? (MMK 3.8)

children.text: vyākhyātaṃ śravaṇaṃ ghrāṇaṃ rasanaṃ sparśanaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing, smelling, tasting, touching, and the mind have been explained

children.text: darśanenaiva jānīyāc chrotṛśrotavyakādi ca // MMK_3.9 //
children.translated_text: by means of seeing alone; one should understand the hearer, the audible, and so forth [in the same way]. (MMK 3.9)

children.text: rūpakāraṇanirmuktaṃ na rūpam upalabhyate /
children.translated_text: Apart from the cause of form, form is not apprehended;

children.text: rūpeṇāpi na nirmuktaṃ dṛśyate rūpakāraṇam // MMK_4.1 //
children.translated_text: nor is the cause of form seen apart from form. (MMK 4.1)

children.text: rūpakāraṇanirmukte rūpe rūpaṃ prasajyate /
children.translated_text: If form were apart from the cause of form, form would follow

children.text: āhetukaṃ na cāsty arthaḥ kaścid āhetukaḥ kva cit // MMK_4.2 //
children.translated_text: as being without a cause; but there is no entity anywhere that is without a cause. (MMK 4.2)

children.text: rūpeṇa tu vinirmuktaṃ yadi syād rūpakāraṇam /
children.translated_text: If the cause of form were to exist apart from form,

children.text: akāryakaṃ kāraṇaṃ syād nāsty akāryaṃ ca kāraṇam // MMK_4.3 //
children.translated_text: the cause would be without an effect; but there is no cause without an effect. (MMK 4.3)

children.text: rūpe saty eva rūpasya kāraṇaṃ nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: When form exists, the cause of form is not tenable;

children.text: rūpe 'saty eva rūpasya kāraṇaṃ nopapadyate // MMK_4.4 //
children.translated_text: when form does not exist, the cause of form is [likewise] not tenable. (MMK 4.4)

children.text: niṣkāraṇaṃ punā rūpaṃ naiva naivopapadyate /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, form without a cause is simply not tenable at all;

children.text: tasmād rūpagatān kāṃścin na vikalpān vikalpayet // MMK_4.5 //
children.translated_text: therefore one should not entertain any conceptions regarding form. (MMK 4.5)

children.text: na kāraṇasya sadṛśaṃ kāryam ity upapadyate /
children.translated_text: It is not tenable that the effect is similar to the cause;

children.text: na kāraṇasyāsadṛśaṃ kāryam ity upapadyate // MMK_4.6 //
children.translated_text: it is not tenable that the effect is dissimilar to the cause. (MMK 4.6)

children.text: vedanācittasaṃjñānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Of feeling, mind, perception,

children.text: sarveṣām eva bhāvānāṃ rūpeṇaiva samaḥ kramaḥ // MMK_4.7 //
children.translated_text: and of formations, and indeed of all entities—the procedure is the same as with form in every respect. (MMK 4.7)

children.text: vigrahe yaḥ parīhāraṃ kṛte śūnyatayā vadet /
children.translated_text: One who would offer a refutation in a debate by [appealing to] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: sarvaṃ tasyāparihṛtaṃ samaṃ sādhyena jāyate // MMK_4.8 //
children.translated_text: for that one everything remains unrefuted, being equivalent to what is to be proved. (MMK 4.8)

children.text: vyākhyāne ya upālambhaṃ kṛte śūnyatayā vadet /
children.translated_text: One who would make a criticism in an explanation by [appealing to] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness),

children.text: sarvaṃ tasyānupālabdhaṃ samaṃ sādhyena jāyate // MMK_4.9 //
children.translated_text: for that one everything remains uncriticized, being equivalent to what is to be proved. (MMK 4.9)

children.text: nākāśaṃ vidyate kiṃcit pūrvam ākāśalakṣaṇāt /
children.translated_text: There is no space (<s>ākāśa</s>) whatsoever prior to the defining characteristic of space;

children.text: alakṣaṇaṃ prasajyeta syāt pūrvaṃ yadi lakṣaṇāt // MMK_5.1 //
children.translated_text: if it existed prior to its characteristic, it would follow that it is without a defining characteristic. (MMK 5.1)

children.text: alakṣaṇo na kaścic ca bhāvaḥ saṃvidyate kva cit /
children.translated_text: No entity whatsoever without a defining characteristic is found anywhere;

children.text: asaty alakṣaṇe bhāve kramatāṃ kuha lakṣaṇam // MMK_5.2 //
children.translated_text: when there is no entity without a characteristic, where does the characteristic proceed to? (MMK 5.2)

children.text: nālakṣaṇe lakṣaṇasya pravṛttir na salakṣaṇe /
children.translated_text: Neither in what is without a characteristic nor in what has a characteristic does the characteristic operate;

children.text: salakṣaṇālakṣaṇābhyāṃ nāpy anyatra pravartate // MMK_5.3 //
children.translated_text: nor does it operate in something other than what has or lacks a characteristic. (MMK 5.3)

children.text: lakṣaṇāsaṃpravṛttau ca na lakṣyam upapadyate /
children.translated_text: When the characteristic does not operate, the characterized is not tenable;

children.text: lakṣyasyānupapattau ca lakṣaṇasyāpy asaṃbhavaḥ // MMK_5.4 //
children.translated_text: when the characterized is not tenable, the characteristic too does not come into being. (MMK 5.4)

children.text: tasmān na vidyate lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ naiva vidyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore, neither the characterized exists, nor does the characteristic exist;

children.text: lakṣyalakṣaṇanirmukto naiva bhāvo 'pi vidyate // MMK_5.5 //
children.translated_text: nor does any entity exist apart from the characterized and the characteristic. (MMK 5.5)

children.text: avidyamāne bhāve ca kasyābhāvo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: When there is no entity, of what will there be non-existence?

children.text: bhāvābhāvavidharmā ca bhāvābhāvāv avaiti kaḥ // MMK_5.6 //
children.translated_text: And who knows that which is different from both entity and non-entity—who knows entity and non-entity? (MMK 5.6)

children.text: tasmānna bhāvo nābhāvo na lakṣyaṃ nāpi lakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Therefore, neither entity, nor non-entity, nor the characterized, nor the characteristic;

children.text: ākāśam ākāśasamā dhātavaḥ pañca ye 'pare // MMK_5.7 //
children.translated_text: space and the other five elements are like space. (MMK 5.7)

children.text: astitvaṃ ye tu paśyanti nāstitvaṃ cālpabuddhayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of little understanding who perceive the existence

children.text: bhāvānāṃ te na paśyanti draṣṭavyopaśamaṃ śivam // MMK_5.8 //
children.translated_text: and non-existence of entities do not see the auspicious pacification of what is to be seen. (MMK 5.8)

children.text: rāgād yadi bhavet pūrvaṃ rakto rāgatiraskṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the one who is attached existed prior to passion, [and] the attached one were independent of passion,

children.text: taṃ pratītya bhaved rāgo rakte rāgo bhavet sati // MMK_6.1 //
children.translated_text: then passion would exist dependent on that attached one—passion would exist when there is an attached one. (MMK 6.1)

children.text: rakte 'sati punā rāgaḥ kuta eva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: When there is no attached one, whence indeed will passion arise?

children.text: sati vāsati vā rāge rakte 'py eṣa samaḥ kramaḥ // MMK_6.2 //
children.translated_text: Whether passion exists or does not exist, the same procedure applies to the attached one too. (MMK 6.2)

children.text: sahaiva punar udbhūtir na yuktā rāgaraktayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Furthermore, simultaneous arising of passion and the attached one is not tenable,

children.text: bhavetāṃ rāgaraktau hi nirapekṣau parasparam // MMK_6.3 //
children.translated_text: for then passion and the attached one would be mutually independent. (MMK 6.3)

children.text: naikatve sahabhāvo 'sti na tenaiva hi tat saha /
children.translated_text: In identity there is no co-existence, for a thing is not together with itself;

children.text: pṛthaktve sahabhāvo 'tha kuta eva bhaviṣyati // MMK_6.4 //
children.translated_text: and in difference, how will co-existence come to be? (MMK 6.4)

children.text: ekatve sahabhāvaś cet syāt sahāyaṃ vināpi saḥ /
children.translated_text: If in identity there were co-existence, it would exist even without a companion;

children.text: pṛthaktve sahabhāvaś cet syāt sahāyaṃ vināpi saḥ // MMK_6.5 //
children.translated_text: if in difference there were co-existence, it would exist even without a companion. (MMK 6.5)

children.text: pṛthaktve sahabhāvaś ca yadi kiṃ rāgaraktayoḥ /
children.translated_text: If co-existence existed in difference, what [would it mean] for passion and the attached one?

children.text: siddhaḥ pṛthakpṛthagbhāvaḥ sahabhāvo yatas tayoḥ // MMK_6.6 //
children.translated_text: Their separate existence would be established, since there is co-existence between them. (MMK 6.6)

children.text: siddhaḥ pṛthakpṛthagbhāvo yadi vā rāgaraktayoḥ /
children.translated_text: If the separate existence of passion and the attached one were indeed established,

children.text: sahabhāvaṃ kimartham tu parikalpayase tayoḥ // MMK_6.7 //
children.translated_text: for what purpose then do you imagine co-existence between them? (MMK 6.7)

children.text: pṛthag na sidhyatīty evaṃ sahabhāvaṃ vikāṅkṣasi /
children.translated_text: Since separate existence is not established—thus you desire co-existence;

children.text: sahabhāvaprasiddhyarthaṃ pṛthaktvaṃ bhūya icchasi // MMK_6.8 //
children.translated_text: for the sake of establishing co-existence, you again desire separateness. (MMK 6.8)

children.text: pṛthagbhāvāprasiddheś ca sahabhāvo na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: Since separate existence is not established, co-existence is not established;

children.text: katamasmin pṛthagbhāve sahabhāvaṃ satīcchasi // MMK_6.9 //
children.translated_text: in which separate existence do you wish co-existence to be present? (MMK 6.9)

children.text: evaṃ raktena rāgasya siddhir na saha nāsaha /
children.translated_text: Thus, the establishment of passion, whether together with or apart from the attached one, is not found;

children.text: rāgavat sarvadharmāṇāṃ siddhir na saha nāsaha // MMK_6.10 //
children.translated_text: like passion, the establishment of all <s>dharmas</s> (entities), whether together with or apart from [their correlates], is not found. (MMK 6.10)

children.text: yadi saṃskṛta utpādas tatra yuktā trilakṣaṇī /
children.translated_text: If arising is conditioned, then the three characteristics are fitting for it;

children.text: athāsaṃskṛta utpādaḥ kathaṃ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇam // MMK_7.1 //
children.translated_text: but if arising is unconditioned, how can it be a characteristic of the conditioned? (MMK 7.1)

children.text: utpādādyās trayo vyastā nālaṃ lakṣaṇakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: The three—arising and the rest—taken separately, are not sufficient for the function of characterizing;

children.text: saṃskṛtasya samastāḥ syur ekatra katham ekadā // MMK_7.2 //
children.translated_text: how could they, taken together, exist simultaneously in a single [entity]? (MMK 7.2)

children.text: utpādasthitibhaṅgānām anyat saṃskṛtalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: If arising, abiding, and perishing have further conditioned characteristics,

children.text: asti ced anavasthaivaṃ nāsti cet te na saṃskṛtāḥ // MMK_7.3 //
children.translated_text: there is an infinite regress; if they do not, they are not conditioned. (MMK 7.3)

children.text: utpādotpāda utpādo mūlotpādasya kevalam /
children.translated_text: The arising of arising is merely the arising of the primary arising;

children.text: utpādotpādam utpādo maulo janayate punaḥ // MMK_7.4 //
children.translated_text: and the primary arising in turn generates the arising of arising. (MMK 7.4)

children.text: utpādotpāda utpādo mūlotpādasya te yadi /
children.translated_text: If, according to you, the arising of arising is the arising of the primary arising,

children.text: maulenājanitas taṃ te sa kathaṃ janayiṣyati // MMK_7.5 //
children.translated_text: how will that [arising of arising], not yet generated by the primary, generate it? (MMK 7.5)

children.text: sa te maulena janito maulaṃ janayate yadi /
children.translated_text: If, according to you, that [arising of arising], generated by the primary, generates the primary,

children.text: maulaḥ sa tenājanitas tam utpādayate katham // MMK_7.6 //
children.translated_text: how does the primary, not yet generated by it, produce it? (MMK 7.6)

children.text: ayam utpādyamānas te kāmam utpādayed imam /
children.translated_text: This one, while being produced, could indeed produce that one,

children.text: yadīmam utpādayitum ajātaḥ śaknuyād ayam // MMK_7.7 //
children.translated_text: if this one, while unborn, were able to produce that one. (MMK 7.7)

children.text: pradīpaḥ svaparātmānau saṃprakāśayate yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a lamp illuminates both itself and others,

children.text: utpādaḥ svaparātmānāv ubhāv utpādayet tathā // MMK_7.8 //
children.translated_text: so too arising would produce both itself and others. (MMK 7.8)

children.text: pradīpe nāndhakāro 'sti yatra cāsau pratiṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the lamp there is no darkness—neither where it is established [nor elsewhere];

children.text: kiṃ prakāśayate dīpaḥ prakāśo hi tamovadhaḥ // MMK_7.9 //
children.translated_text: what does the lamp illuminate? For illumination is the destruction of darkness. (MMK 7.9)

children.text: katham utpadyamānena pradīpena tamo hatam /
children.translated_text: How is darkness destroyed by a lamp that is [still] arising,

children.text: notpadyamāno hi tamaḥ pradīpaḥ prāpnute yadā // MMK_7.10 //
children.translated_text: when the lamp, while arising, does not reach the darkness? (MMK 7.10)

children.text: aprāpyaiva pradīpena yadi vā nihataṃ tamaḥ /
children.translated_text: If, however, darkness is destroyed by a lamp without reaching it,

children.text: ihasthaḥ sarvalokasthaṃ sa tamo nihaniṣyati // MMK_7.11 //
children.translated_text: being here, will destroy the darkness situated in the entire world. // MMK 7.11 //

children.text: pradīpaḥ svaparātmānau saṃprakāśayate yadi /
children.translated_text: If a lamp illuminates both itself and others,

children.text: tamo 'pi svaparātmānau chādayiṣyaty asaṃśayam // MMK_7.12 //
children.translated_text: then darkness too will conceal both itself and others, without doubt. // MMK 7.12 //

children.text: anutpanno 'yam utpādaḥ svātmānaṃ janayet katham /
children.translated_text: This arising, being unarisen, how could it produce itself?

children.text: athotpanno janayate jāte kiṃ janyate punaḥ // MMK_7.13 //
children.translated_text: And if it has already arisen, what is produced again when it is already born? // MMK 7.13 //

children.text: notpadyamānaṃ notpannaṃ nānutpannaṃ kathaṃ cana /
children.translated_text: Neither something in the process of arising, nor something already arisen, nor something not yet arisen

children.text: utpadyate tad ākhyātaṃ gamyamānagatāgataiḥ // MMK_7.14 //
children.translated_text: arises in any way—this has been explained through the analysis of 'the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to.' // MMK 7.14 //

children.text: utpadyamānam utpattāv idaṃ na kramate yadā /
children.translated_text: When the thing in the process of arising does not proceed in the arising,

children.text: katham utpadyamānaṃ tu pratītyotpattim ucyate // MMK_7.15 //
children.translated_text: how can the thing in the process of arising be said to arise dependently? // MMK 7.15 //

children.text: pratītya yad yad bhavati tat tac chāntaṃ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: Whatever arises dependently, that is peaceful by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>);

children.text: tasmād utpadyamānaṃ ca śāntam utpattir eva ca // MMK_7.16 //
children.translated_text: therefore the thing in the process of arising is peaceful, and arising itself is also peaceful. // MMK 7.16 //

children.text: yadi kaścid anutpanno bhāvaḥ saṃvidyate kva cit /
children.translated_text: If some unarisen entity were found to exist somewhere,

children.text: utpadyeta sa kiṃ tasmin bhāva utpadyate 'sati // MMK_7.17 //
children.translated_text: it could arise—but how can an entity arise when it does not exist? // MMK 7.17 //

children.text: utpadyamānam utpādo yadi cotpādayaty ayam /
children.translated_text: If arising produces the thing in the process of arising,

children.text: utpādayet tam utpādam utpādaḥ katamaḥ punaḥ // MMK_7.18 //
children.translated_text: which arising would produce that arising in turn? // MMK 7.18 //

children.text: anya utpādayaty enaṃ yady utpādo 'navasthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: If another arising produces this one, there is an infinite regress;

children.text: athānutpāda utpannaḥ sarvam utpadyatāṃ tathā // MMK_7.19 //
children.translated_text: but if what arises has arisen without arising, then everything could arise in that manner. // MMK 7.19 //

children.text: sataś ca tāvad utpattir asataś ca na yujyate /
children.translated_text: The arising of an existent is untenable, and so is that of a non-existent—

children.text: na sataś cāsataś ceti pūrvam evopapāditam // MMK_7.20 //
children.translated_text: and not of what is both existent and non-existent: this has been established previously. // MMK 7.20 //

children.text: nirudhyamānasyotpattir na bhāvasyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: The arising of an entity that is ceasing is untenable,

children.text: yaś cānirudhyamānas tu sa bhāvo nopapadyate // MMK_7.21 //
children.translated_text: and an entity that is not ceasing is untenable either. // MMK 7.21 //

children.text: nāsthitas tiṣṭhate bhāvaḥ sthito bhāvo na tiṣṭhati /
children.translated_text: An entity that is not abiding does not abide; an entity that has already abided does not abide;

children.text: na tiṣṭhate tiṣṭhamānaḥ ko 'nutpannaś ca tiṣṭhati // MMK_7.22 //
children.translated_text: that which is in the process of abiding does not abide either—and what unarisen thing abides? // MMK 7.22 //

children.text: sthitir nirudhyamānasya na bhāvasyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: The abiding of an entity that is ceasing is untenable,

children.text: yaś cānirudhyamānas tu sa bhāvo nopapadyate // MMK_7.23 //
children.translated_text: and an entity that is not ceasing is also untenable. // MMK 7.23 //

children.text: jarāmaraṇadharmeṣu sarvabhāveṣu sarvadā /
children.translated_text: All entities are at all times subject to aging and death (<s>jarāmaraṇa</s>);

children.text: tiṣṭhanti katame bhāvā ye jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā // MMK_7.24 //
children.translated_text: what entities exist that are free from aging and death? // MMK 7.24 //

children.text: sthityānyayā sthiteḥ sthānaṃ tayaiva ca na yujyate /
children.translated_text: Abiding cannot be established through another abiding or through the same one—

children.text: utpādasya yathotpādo nātmanā na parātmanā // MMK_7.25 //
children.translated_text: just as the arising of arising is neither by itself nor by another. // MMK 7.25 //

children.text: nirudhyate nāniruddhaṃ na niruddhaṃ nirudhyate /
children.translated_text: What has not ceased does not cease; what has already ceased does not cease;

children.text: tathā nirudhyamānaṃ ca kim ajātaṃ nirudhyate // MMK_7.26 //
children.translated_text: nor does what is in the process of ceasing—and how can what is unborn cease? // MMK 7.26 //

children.text: sthitasya tāvad bhāvasya nirodho nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: The cessation of an entity that is abiding is untenable;

children.text: nāsthitasyāpi bhāvasya nirodha upapadyate // MMK_7.27 //
children.translated_text: the cessation of an entity that is not abiding is also untenable. // MMK 7.27 //

children.text: tayaivāvasthayāvasthā na hi saiva nirudhyate /
children.translated_text: A state does not cease by that same state;

children.text: anyayāvasthayāvasthā na cānyaiva nirudhyate // MMK_7.28 //
children.translated_text: nor does a state cease by a different state. // MMK 7.28 //

children.text: yadaiva sarvadharmāṇām utpādo nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: When the arising of all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is untenable,

children.text: tadaivaṃ sarvadharmāṇāṃ nirodho nopapadyate // MMK_7.29 //
children.translated_text: then the cessation of all <s>dharmas</s> is untenable too. // MMK 7.29 //

children.text: sataś ca tāvad bhāvasya nirodho nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: The cessation of an entity that exists is untenable,

children.text: ekatve na hi bhāvaś ca nābhāvaś copapadyate // MMK_7.30 //
children.translated_text: for being and non-being cannot belong to one and the same thing. // MMK 7.30 //

children.text: asato 'pi na bhāvasya nirodha upapadyate /
children.translated_text: The cessation of an entity that does not exist is also untenable—

children.text: na dvitīyasya śirasaś chedanaṃ vidyate yathā // MMK_7.31 //
children.translated_text: just as there is no cutting off of a second head. // MMK 7.31 //

children.text: na svātmanā nirodho 'sti nirodho na parātmanā /
children.translated_text: Cessation does not exist by itself, nor does cessation exist by another—

children.text: utpādasya yathotpādo nātmanā na parātmanā // MMK_7.32 //
children.translated_text: just as the arising of arising is neither by itself nor by another. // MMK 7.32 //

children.text: utpādasthitibhaṅgānām asiddher nāsti saṃskṛtam /
children.translated_text: Since arising, abiding, and destruction are not established, there is no conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>);

children.text: saṃskṛtasyāprasiddhau ca kathaṃ setsyaty asaṃskṛtam // MMK_7.33 //
children.translated_text: and if the conditioned is not established, how will the unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) be established? // MMK 7.33 //

children.text: yathā māyā yathā svapno gandharvanagaraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Like an illusion, like a dream, like a city of <s>Gandharvas</s>—

children.text: tathotpādas tathā sthānaṃ tathā bhaṅga udāhṛtam // MMK_7.34 //
children.translated_text: thus arising, thus abiding, thus destruction have been described. // MMK 7.34 //

children.text: sadbhūtaḥ kārakaḥ karma sadbhūtaṃ na karotyayam /
children.translated_text: An agent that truly exists does not perform an action that truly exists;

children.text: kārako nāpy asadbhūtaḥ karmāsadbhūtam īhate // MMK_8.1 //
children.translated_text: nor does an agent that does not truly exist undertake an action that does not truly exist. // MMK 8.1 //

children.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti karma ca syād akartṛkam /
children.translated_text: A truly existent being has no activity, and the action would be without an agent;

children.text: sadbhūtasya kriyā nāsti kartā ca syād akarmakaḥ // MMK_8.2 //
children.translated_text: a truly existent being has no activity, and the agent would be without an action. // MMK 8.2 //

children.text: karoti yady asadbhūto 'sadbhūtaṃ karma kārakaḥ /
children.translated_text: If a non-existent agent performs a non-existent action,

children.text: ahetukaṃ bhavet karma kartā cāhetuko bhavet // MMK_8.3 //
children.translated_text: the action would be without a cause, and the agent too would be without a cause. // MMK 8.3 //

children.text: hetāv asati kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: In the absence of a cause, neither effect nor cause exists;

children.text: tadabhāve kriyā kartā kāraṇaṃ ca na vidyate // MMK_8.4 //
children.translated_text: in the absence of those, activity, agent, and instrument do not exist. // MMK 8.4 //

children.text: dharmādharmau na vidyete kriyādīnām asaṃbhave /
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit) do not exist when activity and the rest are impossible;

children.text: dharme cāsaty adharme ca phalaṃ tajjaṃ na vidyate // MMK_8.5 //
children.translated_text: and when <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> are absent, their fruit does not exist. // MMK 8.5 //

children.text: phale 'sati na mokṣāya na svargāyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: In the absence of fruit, no path leads to liberation or to heaven;

children.text: mārgaḥ sarvakriyāṇāṃ ca nairarthakyaṃ prasajyate // MMK_8.6 //
children.translated_text: and the purposelessness of all activities would follow. // MMK 8.6 //

children.text: kārakaḥ sadasadbhūtaḥ sadasat kurute na tat /
children.translated_text: An agent that is both existent and non-existent does not perform an action that is both—

children.text: parasparaviruddhaṃ hi sac cāsac caikataḥ kutaḥ // MMK_8.7 //
children.translated_text: for existent and non-existent are mutually contradictory; how can they coexist in one? // MMK 8.7 //

children.text: satā ca kriyate nāsan nāsatā kriyate ca sat /
children.translated_text: An existent does not produce a non-existent, nor does a non-existent produce an existent;

children.text: kartrā sarve prasajyante doṣās tatra ta eva hi // MMK_8.8 //
children.translated_text: in the case of the agent, all the same faults apply. // MMK 8.8 //

children.text: nāsadbhūtaṃ na sadbhūtaḥ sadasadbhūtam eva vā /
children.translated_text: An agent does not perform an action that is non-existent, existent,

children.text: karoti kārakaḥ karma pūrvoktair eva hetubhiḥ // MMK_8.9 //
children.translated_text: or both existent and non-existent—for the very reasons stated before. // MMK 8.9 //

children.text: nāsadbhūto 'pi sadbhūtaṃ sadasadbhūtam eva vā /
children.translated_text: Nor does a non-existent agent perform an action that is existent,

children.text: karoti kārakaḥ karma pūrvoktair eva hetubhiḥ // MMK_8.10 //
children.translated_text: or both existent and non-existent—for the very reasons stated before. // MMK 8.10 //

children.text: karoti sadasadbhūto na san nāsac ca kārakaḥ /
children.translated_text: Nor does an agent that is both existent and non-existent—being neither existent nor non-existent—

children.text: karma tat tu vijānīyāt pūrvoktair eva hetubhiḥ // MMK_8.11 //
children.translated_text: perform that action. This should be understood for the very reasons stated before. // MMK 8.11 //

children.text: pratītya kārakaḥ karma taṃ pratītya ca kārakam /
children.translated_text: Dependently the agent produces the action, and depending on that action

children.text: karma pravartate nānyat paśyāmaḥ siddhikāraṇam // MMK_8.12 //
children.translated_text: the agent operates. We see no other cause for their establishment. // MMK 8.12 //

children.text: evaṃ vidyād upādānaṃ vyutsargād iti karmaṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: In this way one should understand appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>) through the relinquishment of action;

children.text: kartuś ca karmakartṛbhyāṃ śeṣān bhāvān vibhāvayet // MMK_8.13 //
children.translated_text: and through agent and action, one should discern all remaining entities. // MMK 8.13 //

children.text: darśanaśravaṇādīni vedanādīni cāpy atha /
children.translated_text: Seeing, hearing, and the like, and feeling and the rest—

children.text: bhavanti yasya prāg ebhyaḥ so 'stīty eke vadantyuta // MMK_9.1 //
children.translated_text: some say: "He who exists prior to these, that one exists." // MMK 9.1 //

children.text: kathaṃ hy avidyamānasya darśanādi bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How could seeing and the rest belong to something that does not exist?

children.text: bhāvasya tasmāt prāg ebhyaḥ so 'sti bhāvo vyavasthitaḥ // MMK_9.2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, that entity is established as existing prior to these. // MMK 9.2 //

children.text: darśanaśravaṇādibhyo vedanādibhya eva ca /
children.translated_text: That entity which is established as prior to seeing, hearing, and the like,

children.text: yaḥ prāg vyavasthito bhāvaḥ kena prajñapyate 'tha saḥ // MMK_9.3 //
children.translated_text: and prior to feeling and the rest—by what is it then made known? // MMK 9.3 //

children.text: vināpi darśanādīni yadi cāsau vyavasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: If that entity is established even without seeing and the like,

children.text: amūny api bhaviṣyanti vinā tena na saṃśayaḥ // MMK_9.4 //
children.translated_text: then these too will surely exist without it, without doubt. // MMK 9.4 //

children.text: ajyate kenacit kaścit kiṃcit kena cid ajyate /
children.translated_text: Someone is manifested by something; something is manifested by someone.

children.text: kutaḥ kiṃcid vinā kaścit kiṃcit kiṃcid vinā kutaḥ // MMK_9.5 //
children.translated_text: How could someone exist without something, or something without someone? // MMK 9.5 //

children.text: sarvebhyo darśanādibhyaḥ kaścit pūrvo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: No one is found to exist prior to all instances of seeing and the like;

children.text: ajyate darśanādinām anyena punar anyadā // MMK_9.6 //
children.translated_text: rather, through one or another of seeing and the like, at different times, another is manifested. // MMK 9.6 //

children.text: sarvebhyo darśanādibhyo yadi pūrvo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: If no one is found to exist prior to all instances of seeing and the like,

children.text: ekaikasmāt kathaṃ pūrvo darśanādeḥ sa vidyate // MMK_9.7 //
children.translated_text: how could one be found to exist prior to each individual instance of seeing and the like? // MMK 9.7 //

children.text: draṣṭā sa eva sa śrotā sa eva yadi vedakaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the seer is the same as the hearer and the same as the feeler,

children.text: ekaikasmād bhavet pūrvam evaṃ caitan na yujyate // MMK_9.8 //
children.translated_text: it would exist prior to each one, and this is not tenable. // MMK 9.8 //

children.text: draṣṭānya eva śrotānyo vedako 'nyaḥ punar yadi /
children.translated_text: If the seer is different, the hearer different, and the feeler different,

children.text: sati syād draṣṭari śrotā bahutvaṃ cātmanāṃ bhavet // MMK_9.9 //
children.translated_text: when a seer exists there would also be a hearer, and there would be a multiplicity of selves. // MMK 9.9 //

children.text: darśanaśravaṇādīni vedanādīni cāpy atha /
children.translated_text: In the elements from which seeing, hearing, and the like,

children.text: bhavanti yebhyas teṣv eṣa bhūteṣv api na vidyate // MMK_9.10 //
children.translated_text: and feeling and the rest arise—in those elements too, this [self] is not found. // MMK 9.10 //

children.text: darśanaśravaṇādīni vedanādīni cāpy atha /
children.translated_text: If seeing, hearing, and the like, and feeling and the rest

children.text: na vidyate ced yasya sa na vidyanta imāny api // MMK_9.11 //
children.translated_text: do not exist, then he to whom they belong does not exist, and these too do not exist. // MMK 9.11 //

children.text: prāk ca yo darśanādibhyaḥ sāṃprataṃ cordhvam eva ca /
children.translated_text: He who does not exist prior to, simultaneous with, or subsequent to

children.text: na vidyate 'sti nāstīti nivṛttās tatra kalpanāḥ // MMK_9.12 //
children.translated_text: seeing and the like—the conceptual constructions of 'he exists' and 'he does not exist' cease with regard to him. // MMK 9.12 //

children.text: yad indhanaṃ sa ced agnir ekatvaṃ kartṛkarmaṇoḥ /
children.translated_text: If the fuel were the fire, agent and action would be identical;

children.text: anyaś ced indhanād agnir indhanād apy ṛte bhavet // MMK_10.1 //
children.translated_text: if the fire were different from the fuel, it would exist even without fuel. // MMK 10.1 //

children.text: nityapradīpta eva syād apradīpanahetukaḥ /
children.translated_text: It would be eternally burning, and it would have no cause of ignition;

children.text: punarārambhavaiyarthyam evaṃ cākarmakaḥ sati // MMK_10.2 //
children.translated_text: re-ignition would be pointless, and in that case it would be without action. // MMK 10.2 //

children.text: paratra nirapekṣatvād apradīpanahetukaḥ /
children.translated_text: Being independent of anything else, it would have no cause of ignition;

children.text: punarārambhavaiyarthyaṃ nityadīptaḥ prasajyate // MMK_10.3 //
children.translated_text: re-ignition would be pointless, and it would follow that it is eternally burning. // MMK 10.3 //

children.text: tatraitat syād idhyamānam indhanaṃ bhavatīti cet /
children.translated_text: If it is said that what is being kindled is the fuel,

children.text: kenedhyatām indhanaṃ tat tāvanmātram idaṃ yadā // MMK_10.4 //
children.translated_text: by what is the fuel kindled, when it is only fuel at that point? // MMK 10.4 //

children.text: anyo na prāpsyate 'prapto na dhakṣyaty adahan punaḥ /
children.translated_text: What has not reached [the fuel] will not reach it; what has not burned will not burn;

children.text: na nirvāsyaty anirvāṇaḥ sthāsyate vā svaliṅgavān // MMK_10.5 //
children.translated_text: what has not been extinguished will not be extinguished; and it will remain with its own characteristics. // MMK 10.5 //

children.text: anya evandhanād agnir indhanaṃ prāpnuyād yadi /
children.translated_text: If fire, being other than fuel, were to reach the fuel,

children.text: strī saṃprāpnoti puruṣaṃ puruṣaś ca striyaṃ yathā // MMK_10.6 //
children.translated_text: it would be like a woman reaching a man and a man reaching a woman. // MMK 10.6 //

children.text: anya evendhanād agnir indhanaṃ kāmam āpnuyāt /
children.translated_text: If fire, being other than fuel, could indeed reach the fuel,

children.text: agnīndhane yadi syātām anyonyena tiraskṛte // MMK_10.7 //
children.translated_text: it would be only if fire and fuel existed concealing each other mutually. // MMK 10.7 //

children.text: yadīndhanam apekṣyāgnir apekṣyāgniṃ yadīndhanam /
children.translated_text: If fire depends on fuel and fuel depends on fire,

children.text: katarat pūrvaniṣpannaṃ yad apekṣyāgnir indhanam // MMK_10.8 //
children.translated_text: which of the two is established first, that upon which fire depends? // MMK 10.8 //

children.text: yadīndhanam apekṣyāgnir agneḥ siddhasya sādhanam /
children.translated_text: If fire depends on fuel, this would be establishing what is already established;

children.text: evaṃ satīndhanaṃ cāpi bhaviṣyati niragnikam // MMK_10.9 //
children.translated_text: and in that case, the fuel too would exist without fire. // MMK 10.9 //

children.text: yo 'pekṣya sidhyate bhāvas tam evāpekṣya sidhyati /
children.translated_text: If an entity is established in dependence on something, and that very thing is established in dependence on it—

children.text: yadi yo 'pekṣitavyaḥ sa sidhyatāṃ kam apekṣya kaḥ // MMK_10.10 //
children.translated_text: if what is to be depended upon is itself to be established, then what depends on what? // MMK 10.10 //

children.text: yo 'pekṣya sidhyate bhāvaḥ so 'siddho 'pekṣate katham /
children.translated_text: If an entity is established in dependence, how can it, being unestablished, depend?

children.text: athāpy apekṣate siddhas tv apekṣāsya na yujyate // MMK_10.11 //
children.translated_text: And if it depends while already established, then dependence is not tenable for it. // MMK 10.11 //

children.text: apekṣyendhanam agnir na nānapekṣyāgnir indhanam /
children.translated_text: Fire does not depend on fuel, and fire does not not-depend on fuel;

children.text: apekṣyendhanam agniṃ na nānapekṣyāgnim indhanam // MMK_10.12 //
children.translated_text: fuel does not depend on fire, and fuel does not not-depend on fire. // MMK 10.12 //

children.text: āgacchaty anyato nāgnir indhane 'gnir na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Fire does not come from elsewhere; fire is not found in the fuel;

children.text: atrendhane śeṣam uktaṃ gamyamānagatāgataiḥ // MMK_10.13 //
children.translated_text: the rest regarding fuel has been stated through the analysis of 'the being-gone-to, the gone-to, and the not-yet-gone-to.' // MMK 10.13 //

children.text: indhanaṃ punar agnir na nāgnir anyatra cendhanāt /
children.translated_text: The fuel is not the fire, and fire is not other than fuel;

children.text: nāgnir indhanavān nāgnāv indhanāni na teṣu saḥ // MMK_10.14 //
children.translated_text: fire does not possess fuel, and fuels are not in fire, nor is fire in them. // MMK 10.14 //

children.text: agnīndhanābhyāṃ vyākhyāta ātmopādānayoḥ kramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Through fire and fuel, the entire method regarding the self and appropriation (<s>upādāna</s>)

children.text: sarvo niravaśeṣeṇa sārdhaṃ ghaṭapaṭādibhiḥ // MMK_10.15 //
children.translated_text: has been explained, without remainder, together with pot, cloth, and the like. // MMK 10.15 //

children.text: ātmanaś ca satattvaṃ ye bhāvānāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Those who declare a separate real nature (<s>satattva</s>) of the self

children.text: nirdiśanti na tān manye śāsanasyārthakovidān // MMK_10.16 //
children.translated_text: and of entities, each individually—I do not consider them skilled in the meaning of the Teaching. // MMK 10.16 //

children.text: pūrvā prajñāyate koṭir nety uvāca mahāmuniḥ /
children.translated_text: "The prior limit [of <s>saṃsāra</s>] is not discerned"—so said the Great Sage;

children.text: saṃsāro 'navarāgro hi nāsyādir nāpi paścimam // MMK_11.1 //
children.translated_text: for <s>saṃsāra</s> is without beginning or end—it has neither a first nor a last. // MMK 11.1 //

children.text: naivāgraṃ nāvaraṃ yasya tasya madhyaṃ kuto bhavet /
children.translated_text: That which has neither beginning nor end—how could it have a middle?

children.text: tasmān nātropapadyante pūrvāparasahakramāḥ // MMK_11.2 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the sequences of prior, posterior, and simultaneous are not tenable here. // MMK 11.2 //

children.text: pūrvaṃ jātir yadi bhavej jarāmaraṇam uttaram /
children.translated_text: If birth were first and aging-and-death later,

children.text: nirjarā maraṇā jātir bhavej jāyeta cāmṛtaḥ // MMK_11.3 //
children.translated_text: birth would be without aging and death, and one would be born deathless. // MMK 11.3 //

children.text: paścāj jātir yadi bhavej jarāmaraṇam āditaḥ /
children.translated_text: If birth were later and aging-and-death first,

children.text: ahetukam ajātasya syāj jarāmaraṇaṃ katham // MMK_11.4 //
children.translated_text: how could there be aging-and-death—causeless—of one not yet born? // MMK 11.4 //

children.text: na jarāmaraṇaṃ caiva jātiś ca saha yujyate /
children.translated_text: Aging-and-death and birth are not tenable as simultaneous;

children.text: mriyeta jāyamānaś ca syāc cāhetukatobhayoḥ // MMK_11.5 //
children.translated_text: one being born would be dying, and both would be without cause. // MMK 11.5 //

children.text: yatra na prabhavanty ete pūrvāparasahakramāḥ /
children.translated_text: Where these sequences of prior, posterior, and simultaneous

children.text: prapañcayanti tāṃ jātiṃ taj jarāmaraṇaṃ ca kim // MMK_11.6 //
children.translated_text: are not tenable—why do they elaborate about that birth and that aging-and-death? // MMK 11.6 //

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva lakṣyaṃ lakṣaṇam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Effect and cause, the characterized and the characteristic,

children.text: vedanā vedakaś caiva santy arthā ye ca ke cana // MMK_11.7 //
children.translated_text: feeling and the feeler, and whatever other entities there may be— // MMK 11.7 //

children.text: pūrvā na vidyate koṭiḥ saṃsārasya na kevalam /
children.translated_text: not only is the prior limit of <s>saṃsāra</s> not found,

children.text: sarveṣām api bhāvānāṃ pūrvā koṭī na vidyate // MMK_11.8 //
children.translated_text: but the prior limit of all entities whatsoever is not found. // MMK 11.8 //

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtaṃ parakṛtaṃ dvābhyāṃ kṛtam ahetukam /
children.translated_text: Suffering is self-made, made by another, made by both, or without a cause—

children.text: duḥkham ity eka icchanti tac ca kāryaṃ na yujyate // MMK_12.1 //
children.translated_text: some maintain; but that is untenable as an effect. // MMK 12.1 //

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtaṃ yadi bhavet pratītya na tato bhavet /
children.translated_text: If suffering were self-made, it would not arise dependently;

children.text: skandhān imān amī skandhāḥ saṃbhavanti pratītya hi // MMK_12.2 //
children.translated_text: for these aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>) arise in dependence on those aggregates. // MMK 12.2 //

children.text: yady amībhya ime 'nye syur ebhyo vāmī pare yadi /
children.translated_text: If these were different from those, or those were other than these,

children.text: bhavet parakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ parair ebhir amī kṛtāḥ // MMK_12.3 //
children.translated_text: then suffering would be other-made—these being made by those others. // MMK 12.3 //

children.text: svapudgalakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ yadi duḥkhaṃ punar vinā /
children.translated_text: If suffering is made by one's own person (<s>pudgala</s>), then apart from suffering,

children.text: svapudgalaḥ sa katamo yena duḥkhaṃ svayaṃ kṛtam // MMK_12.4 //
children.translated_text: who is that own person by whom suffering is self-made? // MMK 12.4 //

children.text: parapudgalajaṃ duḥkhaṃ yadi yasmai pradīyate /
children.translated_text: If suffering arises from another person, then to whom is it given?

children.text: pareṇa kṛtvā tad duḥkhaṃ sa duḥkhena vinā kutaḥ // MMK_12.5 //
children.translated_text: Having created that suffering, how can he who is without suffering be another? // MMK 12.5 //

children.text: parapudgalajaṃ duḥkhaṃ yadi kaḥ parapudgalaḥ /
children.translated_text: If suffering arises from another person, who is that other person

children.text: vinā duḥkhena yaḥ kṛtvā parasmai prahiṇoti tat // MMK_12.6 //
children.translated_text: who, being without suffering, creates it and sends it to another? // MMK 12.6 //

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtasyāprasiddher duḥkhaṃ parakṛtaṃ kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the self-made is not established, how can suffering be other-made?

children.text: paro hi duḥkhaṃ yat kuryāt tat tasya syāt svayaṃ kṛtam // MMK_12.7 //
children.translated_text: For the suffering that another would make—that for him would be self-made. // MMK 12.7 //

children.text: na tāvat svakṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ na hi tenaiva tat kṛtam /
children.translated_text: Suffering is not self-made, for it is not made by that very thing;

children.text: paro nātmakṛtaś cet syād duḥkhaṃ parakṛtaṃ katham // MMK_12.8 //
children.translated_text: and if the other is not self-made, how can suffering be other-made? // MMK 12.8 //

children.text: syād ubhābhyāṃ kṛtaṃ duḥkhaṃ syād ekaikakṛtaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If suffering could be made by both, it would have to be individually made by each;

children.text: parākārāsvayaṃkāraṃ duḥkham ahetukaṃ kutaḥ // MMK_12.9 //
children.translated_text: not other-made, not self-made—how can suffering be causeless? // MMK 12.9 //

children.text: na kevalaṃ hi duḥkhasya cāturvidhyaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Not only does the fourfold [analysis] not apply to suffering,

children.text: bāhyānām api bhāvānāṃ cāturvidhyaṃ na vidyate // MMK_12.10 //
children.translated_text: but the fourfold [analysis] does not apply to external entities either. // MMK 12.10 //

children.text: tan mṛṣā moṣadharma yad bhagavān ity abhāṣata /
children.translated_text: "That which is deceptive is of a deceptive nature (<s>moṣadharma</s>)"—so the Blessed One declared;

children.text: sarve ca moṣadharmāṇaḥ saṃskārās tena te mṛṣā // MMK_13.1 //
children.translated_text: all conditioned things (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are of a deceptive nature, therefore they are deceptive. // MMK 13.1 //

children.text: tan mṛṣā moṣadharma yad yadi kiṃ tatra muṣyate /
children.translated_text: That which is false, of a deceptive nature—if so, what is deceived therein?

children.text: etat tūktaṃ bhagavatā śūnyatāparidīpakam // MMK_13.2 //
children.translated_text: This, however, was said by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) to illuminate <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). (MMK 13.2)

children.text: bhāvānāṃ niḥsvabhāvatvam anyathābhāvadarśanāt /
children.translated_text: The essencelessness of entities is seen from their becoming otherwise.

children.text: nāsvabhāvaś ca bhāvo 'sti bhāvānāṃ śūnyatā yataḥ // MMK_13.3 //
children.translated_text: There is no entity without essence, since entities are empty. (MMK 13.3)

children.text: kasya syād anyathābhāvaḥ svabhāvaś cen na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Whose alteration would there be if <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) is not found?

children.text: kasya syād anyathābhāvaḥ svabhāvo yadi vidyate // MMK_13.4 //
children.translated_text: Whose alteration would there be if <s>svabhāva</s> is found? (MMK 13.4)

children.text: tasyaiva nānyathābhāvo nāpy anyasyaiva yujyate /
children.translated_text: Alteration of that very thing is not tenable, nor is alteration of another,

children.text: yuvā na jīryate yasmād yasmāj jīrṇo na jīryate // MMK_13.5 //
children.translated_text: since a youth does not age, and since one already aged does not age. (MMK 13.5)

children.text: tasya ced anyathābhāvaḥ kṣīram eva bhaved dadhi /
children.translated_text: If there were alteration of that very thing, milk itself would be curd.

children.text: kṣīrād anyasya kasyacid dadhibhāvo bhaviṣyati // MMK_13.6 //
children.translated_text: Of what other thing than milk would the state of being curd arise? (MMK 13.6)

children.text: yady aśūnyaṃ bhavet kiṃcit syāc chūnyam iti kiṃ cana /
children.translated_text: If something were non-empty, then something would be empty.

children.text: na kiṃcid asty aśūnyaṃ ca kutaḥ śūnyaṃ bhaviṣyati // MMK_13.7 //
children.translated_text: But nothing whatsoever is non-empty—whence then could emptiness arise? (MMK 13.7)

children.text: śūnyatā sarvadṛṣṭīnāṃ proktā niḥsaraṇaṃ jinaiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) has been declared by the Victorious Ones as the escape from all views.

children.text: yeṣāṃ tu śūnyatādṛṣṭis tān asādhyān babhāṣire // MMK_13.8 //
children.translated_text: But those for whom <s>śūnyatā</s> itself is a view—they have been declared incurable. (MMK 13.8)

children.text: draṣṭavyaṃ darśanaṃ draṣṭā trīṇy etāni dviśo dviśaḥ /
children.translated_text: The seen, the seeing, and the seer—these three, taken two by two

children.text: sarvaśaś ca na saṃsargam anyonyena vrajanty uta // MMK_14.1 //
children.translated_text: and in every combination—do not enter into mutual contact. (MMK 14.1)

children.text: evaṃ rāgaś ca raktaś ca rañjanīyaṃ ca dṛśyatām /
children.translated_text: Likewise, let passion, the passionate one, and the object of passion be examined.

children.text: traidhena śeṣāḥ kleśāś ca śeṣāṇy āyatanāni ca // MMK_14.2 //
children.translated_text: The remaining <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and the remaining <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) follow the same threefold pattern. (MMK 14.2)

children.text: anyenānyasya saṃsargas tac cānyatvaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Contact of one with another—but that otherness is not found

children.text: draṣṭavyaprabhṛtīnāṃ yan na saṃsargaṃ vrajanty ataḥ // MMK_14.3 //
children.translated_text: among the seen and the rest; therefore they do not enter into contact. (MMK 14.3)

children.text: na ca kevalam anyatvaṃ draṣṭavyāder na vidyate /
children.translated_text: And it is not only of the seen and the rest that otherness is not found;

children.text: kasyacit kenacit sārdhaṃ nānyatvam upapadyate // MMK_14.4 //
children.translated_text: of anything whatsoever in relation to anything else, otherness is not tenable. (MMK 14.4)

children.text: anyad anyat pratītyānyan nānyad anyad ṛte 'nyataḥ /
children.translated_text: A thing is other only in dependence on another; without the other, it is not other.

children.text: yat pratītya ca yat tasmāt tad anyan nopapadyate // MMK_14.5 //
children.translated_text: And that which depends on something cannot be other than that. (MMK 14.5)

children.text: yady anyad anyad anyasmād anyasmād apy ṛte bhavet /
children.translated_text: If one thing were other than another even apart from that other,

children.text: tad anyad anyad anyasmād ṛte nāsti ca nāsty ataḥ // MMK_14.6 //
children.translated_text: it would be other without the other—but it does not exist without it; therefore it does not exist. (MMK 14.6)

children.text: nānyasmin vidyate 'nyatvam ananyasmin na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Otherness is not found in what is other, nor is it found in what is not other.

children.text: avidyamāne cānyatve nāsty anyad vā tad eva vā // MMK_14.7 //
children.translated_text: And when otherness is not found, there exists neither 'another' nor 'that very thing.' (MMK 14.7)

children.text: na tena tasya saṃsargo nānyenānyasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: Contact of that with that is not tenable, nor of another with another.

children.text: saṃsṛjyamānaṃ saṃsṛṣṭaṃ saṃsraṣṭā ca na vidyate // MMK_14.8 //
children.translated_text: That which is being contacted, the contacted, and the contactor—none are found. (MMK 14.8)

children.text: na saṃbhavaḥ svabhāvasya yuktaḥ pratyayahetubhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The arising of <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature) from causes and conditions is not tenable.

children.text: hetupratyayasaṃbhūtaḥ svabhāvaḥ kṛtako bhavet // MMK_15.1 //
children.translated_text: An own-nature arisen from causes and conditions would be fabricated. (MMK 15.1)

children.text: svabhāvaḥ kṛtako nāma bhaviṣyati punaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: How could there ever be a fabricated own-nature?

children.text: akṛtrimaḥ svabhāvo hi nirapekṣaḥ paratra ca // MMK_15.2 //
children.translated_text: For own-nature is by definition unfabricated and independent of other things. (MMK 15.2)

children.text: kutaḥ svabhāvasyābhāve parabhāvo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: In the absence of own-nature, whence would <s>parabhāva</s> (other-nature) arise?

children.text: svabhāvaḥ parabhāvasya parabhāvo hi kathyate // MMK_15.3 //
children.translated_text: For the own-nature of another entity is called 'other-nature.' (MMK 15.3)

children.text: svabhāvaparabhāvābhyām ṛte bhāvaḥ kutaḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Without own-nature and other-nature, whence could an entity arise?

children.text: svabhāve parabhāve ca sati bhāvo hi sidhyati // MMK_15.4 //
children.translated_text: For an entity is established only when own-nature or other-nature exists. (MMK 15.4)

children.text: bhāvasya ced aprasiddhir abhāvo naiva sidhyati /
children.translated_text: If the existence of an entity is not established, non-existence is also not established.

children.text: bhāvasya hy anyathābhāvam abhāvaṃ bruvate janāḥ // MMK_15.5 //
children.translated_text: For people call the alteration of an entity 'non-existence.' (MMK 15.5)

children.text: svabhāvaṃ parabhāvaṃ ca bhāvaṃ cābhāvam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Those who see own-nature, other-nature, entity, and non-entity

children.text: ye paśyanti na paśyanti te tattvaṃ buddhaśāsane // MMK_15.6 //
children.translated_text: do not see the truth in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching. (MMK 15.6)

children.text: kātyāyanāvavāde cāstīti nāstīti cobhayam /
children.translated_text: In the Instruction to <s>Kātyāyana</s>, both 'it exists' and 'it does not exist'

children.text: pratiṣiddhaṃ bhagavatā bhāvābhāvavibhāvinā // MMK_15.7 //
children.translated_text: were rejected by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, who discerns existence and non-existence. (MMK 15.7)

children.text: yady astitvaṃ prakṛtyā syān na bhaved asya nāstitā /
children.translated_text: If existence were by intrinsic nature, there would be no non-existence of it.

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na hi jātūpapadyate // MMK_15.8 //
children.translated_text: For an alteration of intrinsic nature is never tenable. (MMK 15.8)

children.text: prakṛtau kasya vāsatyām anyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: If intrinsic nature is absent, of what will there be alteration?

children.text: prakṛtau kasya vā satyām anyathātvaṃ bhaviṣyati // MMK_15.9 //
children.translated_text: And if intrinsic nature is present, of what will there be alteration? (MMK 15.9)

children.text: astīti śāśvatagrāho nāstīty ucchedadarśanam /
children.translated_text: 'It exists' is the grasping of eternalism; 'it does not exist' is the view of annihilation.

children.text: tasmād astitvanāstitve nāśrīyeta vicakṣaṇaḥ // MMK_15.10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the wise one should not resort to existence or non-existence. (MMK 15.10)

children.text: asti yad dhi svabhāvena na tan nāstīti śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: That which exists by own-nature does not become non-existent—this is eternalism.

children.text: nāstīdānīm abhūt pūrvam ity ucchedaḥ prasajyate // MMK_15.11 //
children.translated_text: 'It does not exist now but existed before'—this entails annihilation. (MMK 15.11)

children.text: saṃskārāḥ saṃsaranti cen na nityāḥ saṃsaranti te /
children.translated_text: If <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned things) transmigrate, they do not transmigrate as permanent.

children.text: saṃsaranti ca nānityāḥ sattve 'py eṣa samaḥ kramaḥ // MMK_16.1 //
children.translated_text: Nor do impermanent things transmigrate. The same reasoning applies to sentient beings. (MMK 16.1)

children.text: pudgalaḥ saṃsarati cet skandhāyatanadhātuṣu /
children.translated_text: If a <s>pudgala</s> (person) transmigrates among the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), and <s>dhātus</s> (elements),

children.text: pañcadhā mṛgyamāṇo 'sau nāsti kaḥ saṃsariṣyati // MMK_16.2 //
children.translated_text: when sought in five ways that person is not found—who then will transmigrate? (MMK 16.2)

children.text: upādānād upādānaṃ saṃsaran vibhavo bhavet /
children.translated_text: If one transmigrates from appropriation to appropriation, one would be without a self.

children.text: vibhavaś cānupādānaḥ kaḥ sa kiṃ saṃsariṣyati // MMK_16.3 //
children.translated_text: Without a self and without appropriation—who would that be, and what would transmigrate? (MMK 16.3)

children.text: saṃskārāṇāṃ na nirvāṇaṃ kathaṃ cid upapadyate /
children.translated_text: The <s>nirvāṇa</s> of conditioned things is in no way tenable.

children.text: sattvasyāpi na nirvāṇaṃ kathaṃ cid upapadyate // MMK_16.4 //
children.translated_text: The <s>nirvāṇa</s> of a sentient being is also in no way tenable. (MMK 16.4)

children.text: na badhyante na mucyanta udayavyayadharmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Conditioned things that are subject to arising and ceasing

children.text: saṃskārāḥ pūrvavat sattvo badhyate na na mucyate // MMK_16.5 //
children.translated_text: are neither bound nor released. Likewise, a sentient being is neither bound nor released. (MMK 16.5)

children.text: bandhanaṃ ced upādānaṃ sopādāno na badhyate /
children.translated_text: If bondage is <s>upādāna</s> (appropriation), one with appropriation is not bound.

children.text: badhyate nānupādānaḥ kimavastho 'tha badhyate // MMK_16.6 //
children.translated_text: One without appropriation is not bound either—in what state then is one bound? (MMK 16.6)

children.text: badhnīyād bandhanaṃ kāmaṃ bandhyāt pūrvaṃ bhaved yadi /
children.translated_text: Bondage would bind only if it existed prior to the thing to be bound.

children.text: na cāsti tac cheṣam uktaṃ gamyamānagatāgataiḥ // MMK_16.7 //
children.translated_text: But it does not—the rest has been stated by the analysis of 'that being gone to, the gone, and the not-yet-gone.' (MMK 16.7)

children.text: baddho na mucyate tāvad abaddho naiva mucyate /
children.translated_text: A bound one is not released; an unbound one is certainly not released.

children.text: syātāṃ baddhe mucyamāne yugapad bandhamokṣaṇe // MMK_16.8 //
children.translated_text: If a bound one were being released, bondage and release would be simultaneous. (MMK 16.8)

children.text: nirvāsyāmy anupādāno nirvāṇaṃ me bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'I shall attain <s>nirvāṇa</s> without appropriation; <s>nirvāṇa</s> will be mine'—

children.text: iti yeṣāṃ grahas teṣām upādānamahāgrahaḥ // MMK_16.9 //
children.translated_text: those who grasp thus have the greatest grasping of appropriation. (MMK 16.9)

children.text: na nirvāṇasamāropo na saṃsārāpakarṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: Where there is neither the attribution of <s>nirvāṇa</s>

children.text: yatra kas tatra saṃsāro nirvāṇaṃ kiṃ vikalpyate // MMK_16.10 //
children.translated_text: nor the removal of <s>saṃsāra</s>—what there is conceived as <s>saṃsāra</s>, and what as <s>nirvāṇa</s>? (MMK 16.10)

children.text: ātmasaṃyamakaṃ cetaḥ parānugrāhakaṃ ca yat /
children.translated_text: The mind that is self-restrained and that benefits others—

children.text: maitraṃ sa dharamas tad bījaṃ phalasya pretya ceha ca // MMK_17.1 //
children.translated_text: that is friendliness; that is <s>dharma</s>; that is the seed of fruit both hereafter and here. (MMK 17.1)

children.text: cetanā cetayitvā ca karmoktaṃ paramarṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: <s>Cetanā</s> (volition) and what is done after having willed—this the Supreme <s>Ṛṣi</s> called <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tasyānekavidho bhedaḥ karmaṇaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // MMK_17.2 //
children.translated_text: Many kinds of distinctions of that <s>karma</s> have been proclaimed. (MMK 17.2)

children.text: tatra yac cetanety uktaṃ karma tan mānasaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: That which is called 'volition' is considered mental <s>karma</s>.

children.text: cetayitvā ca yat tūktaṃ tat tu kāyikavācikam // MMK_17.3 //
children.translated_text: And what is called 'what is done after having willed'—that is bodily and verbal. (MMK 17.3)

children.text: vāgviṣpando 'viratayo yāś cāvijñaptisaṃjñitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Speech-activity and non-abstentions, and those designated as 'non-informative' (<s>avijñapti</s>),

children.text: avijñaptaya evānyāḥ smṛtā viratayas tathā // MMK_17.4 //
children.translated_text: and other non-informatives, as well as abstentions likewise. (MMK 17.4)

children.text: paribhogānvayaṃ puṇyam apuṇyaṃ ca tathāvidham /
children.translated_text: Merit resulting from enjoyment, and demerit of such a kind,

children.text: cetanā ceti saptaite dharmāḥ karmāñjanāḥ smṛtāḥ // MMK_17.5 //
children.translated_text: and volition—these seven <s>dharmas</s> are remembered as the types of <s>karma</s>. (MMK 17.5)

children.text: tiṣṭhaty ā pākakālāc cet karma tan nityatām iyāt /
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> persists until the time of ripening, it would attain permanence.

children.text: niruddhaṃ cen niruddhaṃ sat kiṃ phalaṃ janayiṣyati // MMK_17.6 //
children.translated_text: And if it has ceased, having ceased, how would it produce a fruit? (MMK 17.6)

children.text: yo 'ṅkuraprabhṛtir bījāt saṃtāno 'bhipravartate /
children.translated_text: The continuum beginning with the sprout proceeds from the seed;

children.text: tataḥ phalam ṛte bījāt sa ca nābhipravartate // MMK_17.7 //
children.translated_text: from that comes the fruit. Without the seed, that continuum does not proceed. (MMK 17.7)

children.text: bījāc ca yasmāt saṃtānaḥ saṃtānāc ca phalodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the continuum comes from the seed, and the fruit arises from the continuum,

children.text: bījapūrvaṃ phalaṃ tasmān nocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam // MMK_17.8 //
children.translated_text: the fruit, preceded by the seed, is therefore neither cut off nor eternal. (MMK 17.8)

children.text: yas tasmāc cittasaṃtānaś cetaso 'bhipravartate /
children.translated_text: Since the mental continuum proceeds from the mind,

children.text: tataḥ phalam ṛte cittāt sa ca nābhipravartate // MMK_17.9 //
children.translated_text: from that comes the fruit. Without the mind, that continuum does not proceed. (MMK 17.9)

children.text: cittāc ca yasmāt saṃtānaḥ saṃtānāc ca phalodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the continuum comes from the mind, and the fruit arises from the continuum,

children.text: karmapūrvaṃ phalaṃ tasmān nocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam // MMK_17.10 //
children.translated_text: the fruit, preceded by <s>karma</s>, is therefore neither cut off nor eternal. (MMK 17.10)

children.text: dharmasya sādhanopāyāḥ śuklāḥ karmapathā daśa /
children.translated_text: The ten white paths of action are the means of accomplishing <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: phalaṃ kāmaguṇāḥ pañca dharmasya pretya ceha ca // MMK_17.11 //
children.translated_text: The five strands of sense-pleasure are the fruit of <s>dharma</s> both hereafter and here. (MMK 17.11)

children.text: bahavaś ca mahāntaś ca doṣāḥ syur yadi kalpanā /
children.translated_text: If this supposition existed, there would be many and great faults.

children.text: syād eṣā tena naivaiṣā kalpanātropapadyate // MMK_17.12 //
children.translated_text: Therefore this supposition is not tenable here. (MMK 17.12)

children.text: imāṃ punaḥ pravakṣyāmi kalpanāṃ yātra yojyate /
children.translated_text: I shall now explain the supposition that is applicable here,

children.text: buddhaiḥ pratyekabuddhaiś ca śrāvakaiś cānuvarṇitām // MMK_17.13 //
children.translated_text: which has been approved by <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>śrāvakas</s>. (MMK 17.13)

children.text: pattraṃ yathā 'vipraṇāśastatharṇam iva karma ca /
children.translated_text: Like an unredeemed promissory note, and like a debt, so is <s>karma</s>.

children.text: caturvidho dhātutaḥ sa prakṛtyāvyākṛtaś ca saḥ // MMK_17.14 //
children.translated_text: It is of four types according to element, and by nature it is morally indeterminate. (MMK 17.14)

children.text: prahāṇato na praheyo bhāvanāheya eva vā /
children.translated_text: It is not to be destroyed by abandonment; it is to be destroyed only by cultivation.

children.text: tasmād avipraṇāśena jāyate karmaṇāṃ phalam // MMK_17.15 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, through the non-destruction [of <s>karma</s>], the fruit of <s>karmas</s> arises. (MMK 17.15)

children.text: prahāṇataḥ praheyaḥ syāt karmaṇaḥ saṃkrameṇa vā /
children.translated_text: If it were to be destroyed by abandonment, or by the transmigration of <s>karma</s>,

children.text: yadi doṣāḥ prasajyeraṃs tatra karmavadhādayaḥ // MMK_17.16 //
children.translated_text: faults such as the destruction of <s>karma</s> would follow. (MMK 17.16)

children.text: sarveṣāṃ visabhāgānāṃ sabhāgānāṃ ca karmaṇām /
children.translated_text: Of all dissimilar and similar <s>karmas</s>,

children.text: pratisaṃdhau sadhātūnām eka utpadyate tu saḥ // MMK_17.17 //
children.translated_text: at the moment of rebirth, a single one of the same element arises. (MMK 17.17)

children.text: karmaṇaḥ karmaṇo dṛṣṭe dharma utpadyate tu saḥ /
children.translated_text: A <s>dharma</s> arises from each and every <s>karma</s> in the present life.

children.text: dviprakārasya sarvasya vipakve 'pi ca tiṣṭhati // MMK_17.18 //
children.translated_text: It persists even when both types have fully ripened. (MMK 17.18)

children.text: phalavyatikramād vā sa maraṇād vā nirudhyate /
children.translated_text: It ceases either through the passing of the fruit or through death.

children.text: anāsravaṃ sāsravaṃ ca vibhāgaṃ tatra lakṣayet // MMK_17.19 //
children.translated_text: One should distinguish therein the division of 'without outflows' (<s>anāsrava</s>) and 'with outflows' (<s>sāsrava</s>). (MMK 17.19)

children.text: śūnyatā ca na cocchedaḥ saṃsāraś ca na śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is not annihilation, and <s>saṃsāra</s> is not eternalism.

children.text: karmaṇo 'vipraṇāśaś ca dharmo buddhena deśitaḥ // MMK_17.20 //
children.translated_text: The non-destruction of <s>karma</s>—this <s>dharma</s> was taught by the <s>Buddha</s>. (MMK 17.20)

children.text: karma notpadyate kasmān niḥsvabhāvaṃ yatas tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Why does <s>karma</s> not arise? Because it is without <s>svabhāva</s> (own-nature).

children.text: yasmāc ca tad anutpannaṃ na tasmād vipraṇaśyati // MMK_17.21 //
children.translated_text: And since it has not arisen, it therefore does not perish. (MMK 17.21)

children.text: karma svabhāvataś cet syāc chāśvataṃ syād asaṃśayam /
