children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> existed by <s>svabhāva</s>, it would undoubtedly be eternal.

children.text: akṛtaṃ ca bhavet karma kriyate na hi śāśvatam // MMK_17.22 //
children.translated_text: And <s>karma</s> would be uncreated, for the eternal is not produced. (MMK 17.22)

children.text: akṛtābhyāgamabhayaṃ syāt karmākṛtakaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> were uncreated, there would be the fear of encountering what was not done.

children.text: abrahmacaryavāsaś ca doṣastatra prasajyate // MMK_17.23 //
children.translated_text: And the fault of not dwelling in the holy life would follow. (MMK 17.23)

children.text: vyavahārā virudhyante sarva eva na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All conventions would be contradicted, without doubt.

children.text: puṇyapāpakṛtor naiva pravibhāgaś ca yujyate // MMK_17.24 //
children.translated_text: And the distinction between the doers of merit and sin would not be tenable. (MMK 17.24)

children.text: tad vipakvavipākaṃ ca punar eva vipakṣyati /
children.translated_text: That whose result has already ripened would ripen yet again.

children.text: karma vyavasthitaṃ yasmāt tasmāt svābhāvikaṃ yadi // MMK_17.25 //
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> would be fixed, if it were therefore by own-nature. (MMK 17.25)

children.text: karma kleśātmakaṃ cedaṃ te ca kleśā na tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If this <s>karma</s> is of the nature of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), and those <s>kleśas</s> are not in reality,

children.text: na cet te tattvataḥ kleśāḥ karma syāt tattvataḥ katham // MMK_17.26 //
children.translated_text: and if those <s>kleśas</s> are not in reality, how could <s>karma</s> be in reality? (MMK 17.26)

children.text: karma kleśāś ca dehānāṃ pratyayāḥ samudāhṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are declared to be the conditions of bodies.

children.text: karma kleśāś ca te śūnyā yadi deheṣu kā kathā // MMK_17.27 //
children.translated_text: If <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are empty, what can be said about bodies? (MMK 17.27)

children.text: avidyānivṛto jantus tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanaś ca saḥ /
children.translated_text: A being is obscured by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) and fettered by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving).

children.text: sa bhoktā sa ca na kartur anyo na ca sa eva saḥ // MMK_17.28 //
children.translated_text: That experiencer is neither different from nor identical with the agent. (MMK 17.28)

children.text: na pratyayasamutpannaṃ nāpratyayasamutthitam /
children.translated_text: Since this <s>karma</s> arises neither from conditions

children.text: asti yasmād idaṃ karma tasmāt kartāpi nāsty ataḥ // MMK_17.29 //
children.translated_text: nor without conditions, therefore there is no agent either. (MMK 17.29)

children.text: karma cen nāsti kartā ca kutaḥ syāt karmajaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: If there is neither <s>karma</s> nor agent, whence would the fruit born of <s>karma</s> arise?

children.text: asaty atha phale bhoktā kuta eva bhaviṣyati // MMK_17.30 //
children.translated_text: And if the fruit does not exist, whence would the experiencer arise? (MMK 17.30)

children.text: yathā nirmitakaṃ śāstā nirmimīta rddhisaṃpadā /
children.translated_text: Just as the Teacher, by the power of supernatural attainment,

children.text: nirmito nirmimītānyaṃ sa ca nirmitakaḥ punaḥ // MMK_17.31 //
children.translated_text: created a magical creation, and that creation created yet another creation, (MMK 17.31)

children.text: tathā nirmitakākāraḥ kartā yat karma tat kṛtam /
children.translated_text: so the agent, having the form of a magical creation—the <s>karma</s> done by him

children.text: tadyathā nirmitenānyo nirmito nirmitas tathā // MMK_17.32 //
children.translated_text: is like another creation created by a creation. (MMK 17.32)

children.text: kleśāḥ karmāṇi dehāś ca kartāraś ca phalāni ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>karmas</s>, bodies, agents, and fruits

children.text: gandharvanagarākārā marīcisvapnasaṃnibhāḥ // MMK_17.33 //
children.translated_text: are like the form of a <s>gandharva</s>-city, like a mirage, like a dream. (MMK 17.33)

children.text: ātmā skandhā yadi bhaved udayavyayabhāg bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the <s>ātman</s> (self) were the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), it would partake of arising and ceasing.

children.text: skandhebhyo 'nyo yadi bhaved bhaved askandhalakṣaṇaḥ // MMK_18.1 //
children.translated_text: If it were other than the <s>skandhas</s>, it would have the character of a non-aggregate. (MMK 18.1)

children.text: ātmany asati cātmīyaṃ kuta eva bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: When the self does not exist, how could 'mine' (<s>ātmīya</s>) exist?

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāraḥ śamād ātmātmanīnayoḥ // MMK_18.2 //
children.translated_text: Free from 'mine' and free from 'I'—through the pacification of self and what belongs to self. (MMK 18.2)

children.text: nirmamo nirahaṃkāro yaś ca so 'pi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: But one who is free from 'I' and 'mine'—that one too is not found.

children.text: nirmamaṃ nirahaṃkāraṃ yaḥ paśyati na paśyati // MMK_18.3 //
children.translated_text: Whoever sees one free from 'I' and 'mine' does not truly see. (MMK 18.3)

children.text: mamety aham iti kṣīṇe bahirdhādhyātmam eva ca /
children.translated_text: When 'mine' and 'I' are extinguished, both externally and internally,

children.text: nirudhyata upādānaṃ tatkṣayāj janmanaḥ kṣayaḥ // MMK_18.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>upādāna</s> (appropriation) ceases; from its destruction comes the destruction of birth. (MMK 18.4)

children.text: karmakleśakṣayān mokṣaḥ karmakleśā vikalpataḥ /
children.translated_text: From the destruction of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> comes <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). <s>Karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> arise from conceptual thought.

children.text: te prapañcāt prapañcas tu śūnyatāyāṃ nirudhyate // MMK_18.5 //
children.translated_text: These arise from <s>prapañca</s> (mental proliferation), and <s>prapañca</s> ceases in <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness). (MMK 18.5)

children.text: ātmety api prajñapitam anātmety api deśitam /
children.translated_text: 'Self' has been designated, and 'non-self' has also been taught.

children.text: buddhair nātmā na cānātmā kaścid ity api deśitam // MMK_18.6 //
children.translated_text: But the <s>Buddhas</s> have also taught that there is neither self nor non-self. (MMK 18.6)

children.text: nivṛttam abhidhātavyaṃ nivṛttaś cittagocaraḥ /
children.translated_text: What is to be expressed has ceased; the domain of mind has ceased.

children.text: anutpannāniruddhā hi nirvāṇam iva dharmatā // MMK_18.7 //
children.translated_text: For <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of things), like <s>nirvāṇa</s>, is without arising and without ceasing. (MMK 18.7)

children.text: sarvaṃ tathyaṃ na vā tathyaṃ tathyaṃ cātathyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Everything is real, or not real, both real and not real,

children.text: naivātathyaṃ naiva tathyam etad buddhānuśāsanam // MMK_18.8 //
children.translated_text: neither not-real nor real—this is the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>. (MMK 18.8)

children.text: aparapratyayaṃ śāntaṃ prapañcair aprapañcitam /
children.translated_text: Not dependent on another, peaceful, not elaborated by <s>prapañca</s> (mental proliferation),

children.text: nirvikalpam anānārtham etat tattvasya lakṣaṇam // MMK_18.9 //
children.translated_text: free from conceptual thought, without distinction—this is the characteristic of <s>tattva</s> (reality). (MMK 18.9)

children.text: pratītya yad yad bhavati na hi tāvat tad eva tat /
children.translated_text: Whatever arises dependently is not thereby that very thing,

children.text: na cānyadapi tattasmānnocchinnaṃ nāpi śāśvatam // MMK_18.10 //
children.translated_text: nor is it something other than that—therefore it is neither annihilated nor eternal. (MMK 18.10)

children.text: anekārtham anānārtham anucchedam aśāśvatam /
children.translated_text: Not of one meaning, not of different meanings, not annihilated, not eternal—

children.text: etat tal lokanāthānāṃ buddhānāṃ śāsanāmṛtam // MMK_18.11 //
children.translated_text: this is the nectar of the teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the Lords of the World. (MMK 18.11)

children.text: saṃbuddhānām anutpāde śrāvakāṇāṃ punaḥ kṣaye /
children.translated_text: When fully enlightened <s>Buddhas</s> do not appear, and when the <s>śrāvakas</s> also have disappeared,

children.text: jñānaṃ pratyekabuddhānām asaṃsargāt pravartate // MMK_18.12 //
children.translated_text: the wisdom of <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> arises independently, without association. (MMK 18.12)

children.text: pratyutpanno 'nāgataś ca yady atītam apekṣya hi /
children.translated_text: If the present and the future depend on the past,

children.text: pratyutpanno 'nāgataś ca kāle 'tīte bhaviṣyataḥ // MMK_19.1 //
children.translated_text: then the present and the future would exist in past time. (MMK 19.1)

children.text: pratyutpanno 'nāgataś ca na stas tatra punar yadi /
children.translated_text: If the present and the future did not exist there,

children.text: pratyutpanno 'nāgataś ca syātāṃ katham apekṣya tam // MMK_19.2 //
children.translated_text: how could the present and the future exist in dependence on it? || MMK 19.2 ||

children.text: anapekṣya punaḥ siddhir nātītaṃ vidyate tayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Again, without dependence [on the past], the establishment of those two does not exist;

children.text: pratyutpanno 'nāgataś ca tasmāt kālo na vidyate // MMK_19.3 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the present and the future — hence time does not exist. || MMK 19.3 ||

children.text: etenaivāvaśiṣṭau dvau krameṇa parivartakau /
children.translated_text: By this same [argument], the remaining two are [refuted] in sequence, with interchange —

children.text: uttamādhamamadhyādīn ekatvādīṃś ca lakṣayet // MMK_19.4 //
children.translated_text: one may characterize the superior, inferior, middle, and the like, as well as oneness and the like. || MMK 19.4 ||

children.text: nāsthito gṛhyate kālaḥ sthitaḥ kālo na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Non-abiding time is not apprehended; abiding time does not exist.

children.text: yo gṛhyetāgṛhītaś ca kālaḥ prajñapyate katham // MMK_19.5 //
children.translated_text: That which is unapprehended — how can time be designated? || MMK 19.5 ||

children.text: bhāvaṃ pratītya kālaś cet kālo bhāvād ṛte kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: If time [exists] depending on an entity, whence is time apart from an entity?

children.text: na ca kaś cana bhāvo 'sti kutaḥ kālo bhaviṣyati // MMK_19.6 //
children.translated_text: And no entity whatsoever exists — whence then will time be? || MMK 19.6 ||

children.text: hetoś ca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryā jāyate yadi /
children.translated_text: If from a cause, from conditions, and from their combination [something] arises —

children.text: phalamasti ca sāmagryāṃ sāmagryā jāyate katham // MMK_20.1 //
children.translated_text: if the fruit already exists in the combination, how does it arise from the combination? || MMK 20.1 ||

children.text: hetoś ca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryā jāyate yadi /
children.translated_text: If from a cause, from conditions, and from their combination [something] arises —

children.text: phalaṃ nāsti ca sāmagryāṃ sāmagryā jāyate katham // MMK_20.2 //
children.translated_text: if the fruit does not exist in the combination, how does it arise from the combination? || MMK 20.2 ||

children.text: hetoś ca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryām asti cet phalam /
children.translated_text: If from a cause and from conditions, the fruit exists in the combination —

children.text: gṛhyeta nanu sāmagryāṃ sāmagryāṃ ca na gṛhyate // MMK_20.3 //
children.translated_text: should it not be apprehended in the combination? But it is not apprehended in the combination. || MMK 20.3 ||

children.text: hetoś ca pratyayānāṃ ca sāmagryāṃ nāsti cet phalam /
children.translated_text: If from a cause and from conditions, the fruit does not exist in the combination —

children.text: hetavaḥ pratyayāś ca syur ahetupratyayaiḥ samāḥ // MMK_20.4 //
children.translated_text: then causes and conditions would be equal to non-causes and non-conditions. || MMK 20.4 ||

children.text: hetuṃ phalasya dattvā ca yadi hetur nirudhyate /
children.translated_text: If the cause ceases after having given [rise to] the fruit of the cause —

children.text: yad dattaṃ yan nirudhaṃ ca hetor ātmadvayaṃ bhavet // MMK_20.5 //
children.translated_text: that which is given and that which ceases — there would be a duality of the cause's self. || MMK 20.5 ||

children.text: hetuṃ phalasyādattvā ca yadi hetur nirudhyate /
children.translated_text: If the cause ceases without having given [rise to] the fruit of the cause —

children.text: hetau niruddhe jātaṃ tat phalam āhetukaṃ bhavet // MMK_20.6 //
children.translated_text: that fruit, arising when the cause has ceased, would be without a cause. || MMK 20.6 ||

children.text: phalaṃ sahaiva sāmagryā yadi prādurbhavet punaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the fruit were to manifest simultaneously with the combination —

children.text: ekakālau prasajyete janako yaś ca janyate // MMK_20.7 //
children.translated_text: it would follow that the producer and that which is produced are simultaneous. || MMK 20.7 ||

children.text: pūrvam eva ca sāmagryāḥ phalaṃ prādurbhaved yadi /
children.translated_text: If the fruit were to manifest prior to the combination —

children.text: hetupratyayanirmuktaṃ phalam āhetukaṃ bhavet // MMK_20.8 //
children.translated_text: the fruit, being devoid of cause and conditions, would be without a cause. || MMK 20.8 ||

children.text: niruddhe cet phalaṃ hetau hetoḥ saṃkramaṇaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If, when the cause has ceased, the fruit [arises] from the cause — there would be a transference of the cause;

children.text: pūrvajātasya hetoś ca punarjanma prasajyate // MMK_20.9 //
children.translated_text: and it would follow that a previously arisen cause is born again. || MMK 20.9 ||

children.text: janayet phalam utpannaṃ niruddho 'staṃgataḥ katham /
children.translated_text: How can [a cause that is] ceased, gone, produce the arisen fruit?

children.text: hetus tiṣṭhann api kathaṃ phalena janayed vṛtaḥ // MMK_20.10 //
children.translated_text: And how can a cause, even while abiding, produce [a fruit] when it is enveloped by the fruit? || MMK 20.10 ||

children.text: athāvṛtaḥ phalenāsau katamaj janayet phalam /
children.translated_text: And if it is not enveloped by the fruit, which fruit would it produce?

children.text: na hy adṛṣṭvā na dṛṣṭvāpi hetur janayate phalam // MMK_20.11 //
children.translated_text: For neither without seeing nor having seen does the cause produce the fruit. || MMK 20.11 ||

children.text: nātītasya hy atītena phalasya saha hetunā /
children.translated_text: Of a past fruit with a past cause —

children.text: nājātena na jātena saṃgatir jātu vidyate // MMK_20.12 //
children.translated_text: neither with an unborn nor with a born [fruit] is there ever a conjunction. || MMK 20.12 ||

children.text: na jātasya hy ajātena phalasya saha hetunā /
children.translated_text: Of a born fruit with a born cause —

children.text: nātītena na jātena saṃgatir jātu vidyate // MMK_20.13 //
children.translated_text: neither with a past nor with a born [fruit] is there ever a conjunction. || MMK 20.13 ||

children.text: nājātasya hi jātena phalasya saha hetunā /
children.translated_text: Of an unborn fruit with a born cause —

children.text: nājātena na naṣṭena saṃgatir jātu vidyate // MMK_20.14 //
children.translated_text: neither with an unborn nor with a perished [fruit] is there ever a conjunction. || MMK 20.14 ||

children.text: asatyāṃ saṃgatau hetuḥ kathaṃ janayate phalam /
children.translated_text: If there is no conjunction, how does the cause produce the fruit?

children.text: satyāṃ vā saṃgatau hetuḥ kathaṃ janayate phalam // MMK_20.15 //
children.translated_text: And if there is conjunction, how does the cause produce the fruit? || MMK 20.15 ||

children.text: hetuḥ phalena śūnyaś cet kathaṃ janayate phalam /
children.translated_text: If the cause is empty of the fruit, how does it produce the fruit?

children.text: hetuḥ phalenāśūnyaś cet kathaṃ janayate phalam // MMK_20.16 //
children.translated_text: If the cause is not empty of the fruit, how does it produce the fruit? || MMK 20.16 ||

children.text: phalaṃ notpatsyate 'śūnyam aśūnyaṃ na nirotsyate /
children.translated_text: A non-empty fruit will not arise; a non-empty [fruit] will not cease;

children.text: aniruddham anutpannam aśūnyaṃ tad bhaviṣyati // MMK_20.17 //
children.translated_text: that non-empty [fruit] would be unceased and unarisen. || MMK 20.17 ||

children.text: katham utpatsyate śūnyaṃ kathaṃ śūnyaṃ nirotsyate /
children.translated_text: How will an empty [fruit] arise? How will an empty [fruit] cease?

children.text: śūnyam apy aniruddhaṃ tad anutpannaṃ prasajyate // MMK_20.18 //
children.translated_text: It follows that the empty too would be unceased and unarisen. || MMK 20.18 ||

children.text: hetoḥ phalasya caikatvaṃ na hi jātūpapadyate /
children.translated_text: Oneness of cause and fruit is never established;

children.text: hetoḥ phalasya cānyatvaṃ na hi jātūpapadyate // MMK_20.19 //
children.translated_text: otherness of cause and fruit is never established. || MMK 20.19 ||

children.text: ekatve phalahetvoḥ syād aikyaṃ janakajanyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: If cause and fruit were one, there would be identity of producer and produced;

children.text: pṛthaktve phalahetvoḥ syāt tulyo hetur ahetunā // MMK_20.20 //
children.translated_text: if cause and fruit were different, the cause would be equal to a non-cause. || MMK 20.20 ||

children.text: phalaṃ svabhāvasadbhūtaṃ kiṃ hetur janayiṣyati /
children.translated_text: A fruit existing by intrinsic nature — what would the cause produce?

children.text: phalaṃ svabhāvāsadbhūtaṃ kiṃ hetur janayiṣyati // MMK_20.21 //
children.translated_text: A fruit not existing by intrinsic nature — what would the cause produce? || MMK 20.21 ||

children.text: na cājanayamānasya hetutvam upapadyate /
children.translated_text: And for that which is not producing, causality is not established;

children.text: hetutvānupapattau ca phalaṃ kasya bhaviṣyati // MMK_20.22 //
children.translated_text: and when causality is not established, whose fruit will there be? || MMK 20.22 ||

children.text: na ca pratyayahetūnām iyam ātmānam ātmanā /
children.translated_text: That combination which does not produce itself by itself

children.text: yā sāmagrī janayate sā kathaṃ janayet phalam // MMK_20.23 //
children.translated_text: from conditions and causes — how would it produce a fruit? || MMK 20.23 ||

children.text: na sāmagrīkṛtaṃ phalaṃ nāsāmagrīkṛtaṃ phalam /
children.translated_text: The fruit is not made by the combination, nor is the fruit made without the combination;

children.text: asti pratyayasāmagrī kuta eva phalaṃ vinā // MMK_20.24 //
children.translated_text: if there is no combination of conditions, whence indeed is the fruit without [it]? || MMK 20.24 ||

children.text: vinā vā saha vā nāsti vibhavaḥ saṃbhavena vai /
children.translated_text: Neither without nor together with arising does destruction exist;

children.text: vinā vā saha vā nāsti saṃbhavo vibhavena vai // MMK_21.1 //
children.translated_text: neither without nor together with destruction does arising exist. || MMK 21.1 ||

children.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nāma vibhavaḥ saṃbhavaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: How indeed would destruction exist without arising?

children.text: vinaiva janma maraṇaṃ vibhavo nodbhavaṃ vinā // MMK_21.2 //
children.translated_text: Without birth there is no death; destruction does not exist without arising. || MMK 21.2 ||

children.text: saṃbhavenaiva vibhavaḥ kathaṃ saha bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How would destruction exist together with arising?

children.text: na janma maraṇaṃ caivaṃ tulyakālaṃ hi vidyate // MMK_21.3 //
children.translated_text: For birth and death do not exist simultaneously. || MMK 21.3 ||

children.text: bhaviṣyati kathaṃ nāma saṃbhavo vibhavaṃ vinā /
children.translated_text: How indeed would arising exist without destruction?

children.text: anityatā hi bhāveṣu na kadācin na vidyate // MMK_21.4 //
children.translated_text: For impermanence is never not found in entities. || MMK 21.4 ||

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavenaiva kathaṃ saha bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How would arising exist together with destruction?

children.text: na janma maraṇaṃ caiva tulyakālaṃ hi vidyate // MMK_21.5 //
children.translated_text: For birth and death do not exist simultaneously. || MMK 21.5 ||

children.text: sahānyonyena vā siddhir vinānyonyena vā yayoḥ /
children.translated_text: For those whose establishment is neither together with each other

children.text: na vidyate tayoḥ siddhiḥ kathaṃ nu khalu vidyate // MMK_21.6 //
children.translated_text: nor without each other — their establishment, how indeed does it exist? || MMK 21.6 ||

children.text: kṣayasya saṃbhavo nāsti nākṣayasyāsti saṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no arising of what is decaying; there is no arising of what is not decaying;

children.text: kṣayasya vibhavo nāsti vibhavo nākṣayasya ca // MMK_21.7 //
children.translated_text: there is no destruction of what is decaying; there is no destruction of what is not decaying. || MMK 21.7 ||

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaś caiva vinā bhāvaṃ na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Arising and destruction do not exist without an entity;

children.text: saṃbhavaṃ vibhavaṃ caiva vinā bhāvo na vidyate // MMK_21.8 //
children.translated_text: an entity does not exist without arising and destruction. || MMK 21.8 ||

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaś caiva na śūnyasyopapadyate /
children.translated_text: Arising and destruction are not established for what is empty;

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaś caiva nāśūnyasyopapadyate // MMK_21.9 //
children.translated_text: arising and destruction are not established for what is non-empty. || MMK 21.9 ||

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaś caiva naika ity upapadyate /
children.translated_text: Arising and destruction are not established as one;

children.text: saṃbhavo vibhavaś caiva na nānety upapadyate // MMK_21.10 //
children.translated_text: arising and destruction are not established as different. || MMK 21.10 ||

children.text: dṛśyate saṃbhavaścaiva vibhavaś caiva te bhavet /
children.translated_text: If you think that arising and destruction are seen —

children.text: dṛśyate saṃbhavaścaiva mohād vibhava eva ca // MMK_21.11 //
children.translated_text: arising and destruction are seen only through delusion. || MMK 21.11 ||

children.text: na bhāvāj jāyate bhāvo bhāvo 'bhāvān na jāyate /
children.translated_text: An entity does not arise from an entity; an entity does not arise from a non-entity;

children.text: nābhāvāj jāyate 'bhāvo 'bhāvo bhāvān na jāyate // MMK_21.12 //
children.translated_text: a non-entity does not arise from a non-entity; a non-entity does not arise from an entity. || MMK 21.12 ||

children.text: na svato jāyate bhāvaḥ parato naiva jāyate /
children.translated_text: An entity does not arise from itself; it does not arise from another;

children.text: na svataḥ parataś caiva jāyate jāyate kutaḥ // MMK_21.13 //
children.translated_text: it does not arise from itself and another — whence then does it arise? || MMK 21.13 ||

children.text: bhāvam abhyupapannasya śāśvatocchedadarśanam /
children.translated_text: For one who accepts an entity, the views of eternalism and annihilationism

children.text: prasajyate sa bhāvo hi nityo 'nityo 'tha vā bhavet // MMK_21.14 //
children.translated_text: follow — for that entity would be either permanent or impermanent. || MMK 21.14 ||

children.text: bhāvam abhyupapannasya naivocchedo na śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: For one who accepts an entity, [there is] neither annihilationism nor eternalism —

children.text: udayavyayasaṃtānaḥ phalahetvor bhavaḥ sa hi // MMK_21.15 //
children.translated_text: for existence is the continuum of arising and destruction of cause and fruit. || MMK 21.15 ||

children.text: udayavyayasaṃtānaḥ phalahetvor bhavaḥ sa cet /
children.translated_text: If existence is the continuum of arising and destruction of cause and fruit —

children.text: vyayasyāpunarutpatter hetūcchedaḥ prasajyate // MMK_21.16 //
children.translated_text: since what has ceased does not arise again, the annihilation of the cause follows. || MMK 21.16 ||

children.text: sadbhāvasya svabhāvena nāsadbhāvaś ca yujyate /
children.translated_text: For what exists with intrinsic nature, non-existence is not appropriate;

children.text: nirvāṇakāle cocchedaḥ praśamād bhavasaṃtateḥ // MMK_21.17 //
children.translated_text: and at the time of <s>nirvāṇa</s>, there would be annihilation through the cessation of the continuum of existence. || MMK 21.17 ||

children.text: carame na niruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the last [moment] has not ceased, the first existence is not established;

children.text: carame nāniruddhe ca prathamo yujyate bhavaḥ // MMK_21.18 //
children.translated_text: if the last [moment] has not not-ceased, the first existence is [still] not established. || MMK 21.18 ||

children.text: nirudhyamāne carame prathamo yadi jāyate /
children.translated_text: If while the last is ceasing the first arises —

children.text: nirudhyamāna ekaḥ syāj jāyamāno 'paro bhavet // MMK_21.19 //
children.translated_text: the one ceasing would be one thing, and the one arising would be another. || MMK 21.19 ||

children.text: na cen nirudhyamānaś ca jāyamānaś ca yujyate /
children.translated_text: If the ceasing and the arising are not coherent,

children.text: sārdhaṃ ca mriyate yeṣu teṣu skandheṣu jāyate // MMK_21.20 //
children.translated_text: [then one] dies in those very aggregates in which one is born. || MMK 21.20 ||

children.text: evaṃ triṣv api kāleṣu na yuktā bhavasaṃtatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus in all three times, the continuum of existence is not coherent;

children.text: triṣu kāleṣu yā nāsti sā kathaṃ bhavasaṃtatiḥ // MMK_21.21 //
children.translated_text: that which does not exist in the three times — how is it a continuum of existence? || MMK 21.21 ||

children.text: skandhā na nānyaḥ skandhebhyo nāsmin skandhā na teṣu saḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is not the aggregates, not other than the aggregates; the aggregates are not in him, nor he in them;

children.text: tathāgataḥ skandhavān na katamo 'tra tathāgataḥ // MMK_22.1 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s> does not possess the aggregates — what then is the <s>Tathāgata</s>? || MMK 22.1 ||

children.text: buddhaḥ skandhān upādāya yadi nāsti svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If the <s>Buddha</s> does not exist by intrinsic nature in dependence on the aggregates,

children.text: svabhāvataś ca yo nāsti kutaḥ sa parabhāvataḥ // MMK_22.2 //
children.translated_text: and what does not exist by intrinsic nature — whence would it exist by other-nature? || MMK 22.2 ||

children.text: pratītya parabhāvaṃ yaḥ so 'nātmety upapadyate /
children.translated_text: That which depends on other-nature — it is established as being without self;

children.text: yaś cānātmā sa ca kathaṃ bhaviṣyati tathāgataḥ // MMK_22.3 //
children.translated_text: and that which is without self — how will it be the <s>Tathāgata</s>? || MMK 22.3 ||

children.text: yadi nāsti svabhāvaś ca parabhāvaḥ kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If there is no intrinsic nature, how would there be other-nature?

children.text: svabhāvaparabhāvābhyām ṛte kaḥ sa tathāgataḥ // MMK_22.4 //
children.translated_text: Without intrinsic nature and other-nature, what <s>Tathāgata</s> is there? || MMK 22.4 ||

children.text: skandhān yady anupādāya bhavet kaścit tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: If some <s>Tathāgata</s> were to exist without appropriating the aggregates,

children.text: sa idānīm upādadyād upādāya tato bhavet // MMK_22.5 //
children.translated_text: then he would now appropriate — and [only] by appropriating would he exist. || MMK 22.5 ||

children.text: skandhāṃś cāpy anupādāya nāsti kaścit tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: But there is no <s>Tathāgata</s> whatsoever without appropriating the aggregates;

children.text: yaś ca nāsty anupādāya sa upādāsyate katham // MMK_22.6 //
children.translated_text: and one who does not exist without appropriating — how would he appropriate? || MMK 22.6 ||

children.text: na bhavaty anupādattam upādānaṃ ca kiṃ cana /
children.translated_text: There is nothing whatsoever that is appropriation without being appropriated;

children.text: na cāsti nirupādānaḥ kathaṃ cana tathāgataḥ // MMK_22.7 //
children.translated_text: and there is no <s>Tathāgata</s> in any way without appropriation. || MMK 22.7 ||

children.text: tattvānyatvena yo nāsti mṛgyamāṇaś ca pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: That which, when sought in five ways, does not exist as identical or different [from the aggregates] —

children.text: upādānena sa kathaṃ prajñapyate tathāgataḥ // MMK_22.8 //
children.translated_text: how can that <s>Tathāgata</s> be designated through appropriation? || MMK 22.8 ||

children.text: yad apīdam upādānaṃ tat svabhāvān na vidyate /
children.translated_text: Moreover, this appropriation does not exist by intrinsic nature;

children.text: svabhāvataś ca yan nāsti kutas tat parabhāvataḥ // MMK_22.9 //
children.translated_text: and what does not exist by intrinsic nature — whence would it exist by other-nature? || MMK 22.9 ||

children.text: evaṃ śūnyam upādānam upādātā ca sarvaśaḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, appropriation is empty and the appropriator is [empty] in every way;

children.text: prajñapyate ca śūnyena kathaṃ śūnyas tathāgataḥ // MMK_22.10 //
children.translated_text: how is the empty <s>Tathāgata</s> designated by what is empty? || MMK 22.10 ||

children.text: śūnyam iti na vaktavyam aśūnyam iti vā bhavet /
children.translated_text: It should not be said 'empty,' nor should it be 'non-empty,'

children.text: ubhayaṃ nobhayaṃ ceti prajñaptyarthaṃ tu kathyate // MMK_22.11 //
children.translated_text: nor both, nor neither — [these] are said for the purpose of designation. || MMK 22.11 ||

children.text: śāśvatāśāśvatādy atra kutaḥ śānte catuṣṭayam /
children.translated_text: Whence [could] the fourfold [alternatives of] eternalism, non-eternalism, etc. [apply] to one who is at peace?

children.text: antānantādi cāpy atra kutaḥ śānte catuṣṭayam // MMK_22.12 //
children.translated_text: And whence [could] the fourfold [alternatives of] finite, infinite, etc. [apply] to one who is at peace? || MMK 22.12 ||

children.text: ghanagrāho gṛhītas tu yenāstīti tathāgataḥ /
children.translated_text: One who holds the dense grasping 'The <s>Tathāgata</s> exists' —

children.text: nāstīti sa vikalpayan nirvṛtasyāpi kalpayet // MMK_22.13 //
children.translated_text: conceptualizing 'He does not exist,' would conceptualize even about one who has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>. || MMK 22.13 ||

children.text: svabhāvataś ca śūnye 'smiṃś cintā naivopapadyate /
children.translated_text: Regarding this one who is empty by intrinsic nature, the thought does not arise at all:

children.text: paraṃ nirodhād bhavati buddho na bhavatīti vā // MMK_22.14 //
children.translated_text: 'After cessation, the <s>Buddha</s> exists' or 'does not exist.' || MMK 22.14 ||

children.text: prapañcayanti ye buddhaṃ prapañcātītam avyayam /
children.translated_text: Those who elaborate upon the <s>Buddha</s>, who is beyond elaboration and imperishable —

children.text: te prapañcahatāḥ sarve na paśyanti tathāgatam // MMK_22.15 //
children.translated_text: all of them, destroyed by elaboration, do not see the <s>Tathāgata</s>. || MMK 22.15 ||

children.text: tathāgato yatsvabhāvas tatsvabhāvam idaṃ jagat /
children.translated_text: Whatever is the intrinsic nature of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that is the intrinsic nature of this world;

children.text: tathāgato niḥsvabhāvo niḥsvabhāvam idaṃ jagat // MMK_22.16 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Tathāgata</s> is without intrinsic nature — this world is without intrinsic nature. || MMK 22.16 ||

children.text: saṃkalpaprabhavo rāgo dveṣo mohaś ca kathyate /
children.translated_text: Desire is said to arise from conceptualization, as do hatred and delusion;

children.text: śubhāśubhaviparyāsān saṃbhavanti pratītya hi // MMK_23.1 //
children.translated_text: for they arise in dependence on the agreeable, the disagreeable, and error. || MMK 23.1 ||

children.text: śubhāśubhaviparyāsān saṃbhavanti pratītya ye /
children.translated_text: Those which arise in dependence on the agreeable, the disagreeable, and error —

children.text: te svabhāvān na vidyante tasmāt kleśā na tattvataḥ // MMK_23.2 //
children.translated_text: they do not exist by intrinsic nature; therefore the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are not [real] in truth. || MMK 23.2 ||

children.text: ātmano 'stitvanāstitve na kathaṃ cic ca sidhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: The existence and non-existence of the self are in no way established;

children.text: taṃ vināstitvanāstitve kleśānāṃ sidhyataḥ katham // MMK_23.3 //
children.translated_text: without that, how are the existence and non-existence of the <s>kleśas</s> established? || MMK 23.3 ||

children.text: kasya cid dhi bhavantīme kleśāḥ sa ca na sidhyati /
children.translated_text: These <s>kleśas</s> belong to someone — but that [someone] is not established;

children.text: kaścid āho vinā kaṃcit santi kleśā na kasyacit // MMK_23.4 //
children.translated_text: without someone, indeed, <s>kleśas</s> do not belong to anyone. || MMK 23.4 ||

children.text: svakāyadṛṣṭivat kleśāḥ kliṣṭe santi na pañcadhā /
children.translated_text: Like the self-view (<s>svakāyadṛṣṭi</s>), the <s>kleśas</s> do not exist in the afflicted one in five ways;

children.text: svakāyadṛṣṭivat kliṣṭaṃ kleśeṣv api na pañcadhā // MMK_23.5 //
children.translated_text: like the self-view, the afflicted one does not exist in the <s>kleśas</s> in five ways. || MMK 23.5 ||

children.text: svabhāvato na vidyante śubhāśubhaviparyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: The errors regarding the agreeable and disagreeable do not exist by intrinsic nature;

children.text: pratītya katamān kleśāḥ śubhāśubhaviparyayān // MMK_23.6 //
children.translated_text: depending on which errors regarding the agreeable and disagreeable do the <s>kleśas</s> [arise]? || MMK 23.6 ||

children.text: rūpaśabdarasasparśā gandhā dharmāś ca ṣaḍvidham /
children.translated_text: Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and <s>dharmas</s> — these six kinds

children.text: vastu rāgasya doṣasya mohasya ca vikalpyate // MMK_23.7 //
children.translated_text: of objects are imagined [as the basis] of desire, hatred, and delusion. || MMK 23.7 ||

children.text: rūpaśabdarasasparśā gandhā dharmāś ca kevalāḥ /
children.translated_text: Form, sound, taste, touch, smell, and <s>dharmas</s> are mere [appearances] —

children.text: gandharvanagarākārā marīcisvapnasaṃnibhāḥ // MMK_23.8 //
children.translated_text: like the form of a <s>Gandharva</s>-city, resembling a mirage or a dream. || MMK 23.8 ||

children.text: aśubhaṃ vā śubhaṃ vāpi kutas teṣu bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How would the disagreeable or the agreeable exist in those

children.text: māyāpuruṣakalpeṣu pratibimbasameṣu ca // MMK_23.9 //
children.translated_text: which are like illusory persons, like reflections? || MMK 23.9 ||

children.text: anapekṣya śubhaṃ nāsty aśubhaṃ prajñapayemahi /
children.translated_text: Without dependence on the agreeable, the disagreeable does not exist — so we assert;

children.text: yat pratītya śubhaṃ tasmāc chubhaṃ naivopapadyate // MMK_23.10 //
children.translated_text: since the agreeable is dependent [on the disagreeable], the agreeable itself is not established. || MMK 23.10 ||

children.text: anapekṣyāśubhaṃ nāsti śubhaṃ prajñapayemahi /
children.translated_text: Without dependence on the disagreeable, the agreeable does not exist — so we assert;

children.text: yat pratītyāśubhaṃ tasmād aśubhaṃ naiva vidyate // MMK_23.11 //
children.translated_text: since the disagreeable is dependent [on the agreeable], the disagreeable itself does not exist. || MMK 23.11 ||

children.text: avidyamāne ca śubhe kuto rāgo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: When the agreeable does not exist, whence will desire arise?

children.text: aśubhe 'vidyamāne ca kuto dveṣo bhaviṣyati // MMK_23.12 //
children.translated_text: When the disagreeable does not exist, whence will hatred arise? || MMK 23.12 ||

children.text: anitye nityam ity evaṃ yadi grāho viparyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If grasping 'permanent' regarding what is impermanent is an error —

children.text: nānityaṃ vidyate śūnye kuto grāho viparyayaḥ // MMK_23.13 //
children.translated_text: since nothing impermanent exists in [what is] empty, whence is the grasping [that constitutes] error? || MMK 23.13 ||

children.text: anitye nityam ity evaṃ yadi grāho viparyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If grasping 'permanent' regarding what is impermanent is an error —

children.text: anityam ity api grāhaḥ śūnye kiṃ na viparyayaḥ // MMK_23.14 //
children.translated_text: is not the grasping 'impermanent' also an error in [what is] empty? || MMK 23.14 ||

children.text: yena gṛhṇāti yo grāho grahītā yac ca gṛhyate /
children.translated_text: That by which one grasps, the grasping, the grasper, and what is grasped —

children.text: upaśāntāni sarvāṇi tasmād grāho na vidyate // MMK_23.15 //
children.translated_text: all are at peace; therefore grasping does not exist. || MMK 23.15 ||

children.text: avidyamāne grāhe ca mithyā vā samyag eva vā /
children.translated_text: When grasping does not exist — whether false or correct —

children.text: bhaved viparyayaḥ kasya bhavet kasyāviparyayaḥ // MMK_23.16 //
children.translated_text: whose error would there be? Whose non-error would there be? || MMK 23.16 ||

children.text: na cāpi viparītasya saṃbhavanti viparyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: And errors do not arise for one who is in error;

children.text: na cāpy aviparītasya saṃbhavanti viparyayāḥ // MMK_23.17 //
children.translated_text: and errors do not arise for one who is not in error. || MMK 23.17 ||

children.text: na viparyasyamānasya saṃbhavanti viparyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: Errors do not arise for one who is [in the process of] erring;

children.text: vimṛśasva svayaṃ kasya saṃbhavanti viparyayāḥ // MMK_23.18 //
children.translated_text: examine yourself — for whom do errors arise? || MMK 23.18 ||

children.text: anutpannāḥ kathaṃ nāma bhaviṣyanti viparyayāḥ /
children.translated_text: How indeed will perversions come into being when they are unborn?

children.text: viparyayeṣv ajāteṣu viparyayagataḥ kutaḥ // MMK_23.19 //
children.translated_text: When perversions are unborn, whence comes one gone to perversion?

children.text: na svato jāyate bhāvaḥ parato naiva jāyate /
children.translated_text: A thing does not arise from itself, nor does it arise from another;

children.text: na svataḥ parataś ceti viparyayagataḥ kutaḥ // MMK_23.20 //
children.translated_text: nor from both self and other—whence then one gone to perversion?

children.text: ātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca yadi vidyate /
children.translated_text: If self, purity, permanence, and happiness exist,

children.text: ātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca na viparyayaḥ // MMK_23.21 //
children.translated_text: then self, purity, permanence, and happiness are not perversions.

children.text: nātmā ca śuci nityaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca yadi vidyate /
children.translated_text: If self, purity, permanence, and happiness do not exist,

children.text: anātmā 'śucy anityaṃ ca naiva duḥkhaṃ ca vidyate // MMK_23.22 //
children.translated_text: then non-self, impurity, impermanence, and suffering likewise do not exist.

children.text: evaṃ nirudhyate 'vidyā viparyayanirodhanāt /
children.translated_text: Thus <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) ceases through the cessation of perversions;

children.text: avidyāyāṃ niruddhāyāṃ saṃskārādyaṃ nirudhyate // MMK_23.23 //
children.translated_text: when <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) and the rest cease.

children.text: yadi bhūtāḥ svabhāvena kleśāḥ kecid dhi kasyacit /
children.translated_text: If indeed certain <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of anyone truly exist by own-nature,

children.text: kathaṃ nāma prahīyeran kaḥ svabhāvaṃ prahāsyati // MMK_23.24 //
children.translated_text: how could they ever be abandoned? Who will abandon own-nature?

children.text: yady abhūtāḥ svabhāvena kleśāḥ kecid dhi kasyacit /
children.translated_text: If indeed certain <s>kleśas</s> of anyone do not truly exist by own-nature,

children.text: kathaṃ nāma prahīyeran ko 'sadbhāvaṃ prahāsyati // MMK_23.25 //
children.translated_text: how could they ever be abandoned? Who will abandon what does not exist?

children.text: yadi śūnyam idaṃ sarvam udayo nāsti na vyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all this is empty, there is no arising and no passing away;

children.text: caturṇām āryasatyānām abhāvas te prasajyate // MMK_24.1 //
children.translated_text: it follows for you that the four Noble Truths are non-existent.

children.text: parijñā ca prahāṇaṃ ca bhāvanā sākṣikarma ca /
children.translated_text: Full understanding, abandonment, cultivation, and direct realization—

children.text: caturṇām āryasatyānām abhāvān nopapadyate // MMK_24.2 //
children.translated_text: from the non-existence of the four Noble Truths, these are not possible.

children.text: tadabhāvān na vidyante catvāry āryaphalāni ca /
children.translated_text: In their absence, the four noble fruits also do not exist;

children.text: phalābhāve phalasthā no na santi pratipannakāḥ // MMK_24.3 //
children.translated_text: without fruits, there are no attainers of fruits, nor those who have entered the path.

children.text: saṃgho nāsti na cet santi te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ /
children.translated_text: If those eight types of persons do not exist, the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not exist;

children.text: abhāvāc cāryasatyānāṃ saddharmo 'pi na vidyate // MMK_24.4 //
children.translated_text: and from the non-existence of the Noble Truths, the true <s>Dharma</s> also does not exist.

children.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: And if neither <s>Dharma</s> nor <s>Saṃgha</s> exist, how can there be a <s>Buddha</s>?

children.text: evaṃ trīṇy api ratnāni bruvāṇaḥ pratibādhase // MMK_24.5 //
children.translated_text: Speaking thus, you deny the Three Jewels.

children.text: śūnyatāṃ phalasadbhāvam adharmaṃ dharmam eva ca /
children.translated_text: [You deny] <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), the existence of fruits, <s>adharma</s> and <s>dharma</s> itself,

children.text: sarvasaṃvyavahārāṃś ca laukikān pratibādhase // MMK_24.6 //
children.translated_text: and all worldly conventions.

children.text: atra brūmaḥ śūnyatāyāṃ na tvaṃ vetsi prayojanam /
children.translated_text: To this we reply: you do not understand the purpose of <s>śūnyatā</s>,

children.text: śūnyatāṃ śūnyatārthaṃ ca tata evaṃ vihanyase // MMK_24.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>śūnyatā</s> itself, nor the meaning of <s>śūnyatā</s>; therefore you are thus afflicted.

children.text: dve satye samupāśritya buddhānāṃ dharmadeśanā /
children.translated_text: The teaching of <s>Dharma</s> by the <s>Buddhas</s> is based upon two truths:

children.text: lokasaṃvṛtisatyaṃ ca satyaṃ ca paramārthataḥ // MMK_24.8 //
children.translated_text: the conventional truth of the world, and truth in the ultimate sense.

children.text: ye 'nayor na vijānanti vibhāgaṃ satyayor dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who do not understand the distinction

children.text: te tattvaṃ na vijānanti gambhīraṃ buddhaśāsane // MMK_24.9 //
children.translated_text: between these two truths do not understand the profound reality in the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching.

children.text: vyavahāram anāśritya paramārtho na deśyate /
children.translated_text: Without relying on convention, the ultimate truth cannot be taught;

children.text: paramārtham anāgamya nirvāṇaṃ nādhigamyate // MMK_24.10 //
children.translated_text: without arriving at the ultimate truth, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained.

children.text: vināśayati durdṛṣtā śūnyatā mandamedhasam /
children.translated_text: Wrongly perceived, <s>śūnyatā</s> destroys one of dull intelligence,

children.text: sarpo yathā durgṛhīto vidyā vā duṣprasādhitā // MMK_24.11 //
children.translated_text: like a serpent wrongly grasped, or a spell wrongly practiced.

children.text: ataś ca pratyudāvṛttaṃ cittaṃ deśayituṃ muneḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore the mind of the Sage turned away from

children.text: dharmaṃ matvāsya dharmasya mandair duravagāhatām // MMK_24.12 //
children.translated_text: teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, knowing the difficulty of this <s>Dharma</s> being fathomed by the dull-witted.

children.text: śūnyatāyām adhilayaṃ yaṃ punaḥ kurute bhavān /
children.translated_text: Whatever objection you raise against <s>śūnyatā</s>,

children.text: doṣaprasaṅgo nāsmākaṃ sa śūnye nopapadyate // MMK_24.13 //
children.translated_text: that charge does not apply to us; it is not applicable to emptiness.

children.text: sarvaṃ ca yujyate tasya śūnyatā yasya yujyate /
children.translated_text: For one for whom <s>śūnyatā</s> is coherent, everything is coherent;

children.text: sarvaṃ na yujyate tasya śūnyaṃ yasya na yujyate // MMK_24.14 //
children.translated_text: for one for whom <s>śūnyatā</s> is not coherent, nothing is coherent.

children.text: sa tvaṃ doṣān ātmanīyān asmāsu paripātayan /
children.translated_text: You, projecting your own faults onto us—

children.text: aśvam evābhirūḍhaḥ sann aśvam evāsi vismṛtaḥ // MMK_24.15 //
children.translated_text: it is as if, having mounted a horse, you have forgotten that very horse.

children.text: svabhāvād yadi bhāvānāṃ sadbhāvam anupaśyasi /
children.translated_text: If you perceive the existence of things by own-nature,

children.text: ahetupratyayān bhāvāṃs tvam evaṃ sati paśyasi // MMK_24.16 //
children.translated_text: then you perceive things as without causes and conditions.

children.text: kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ caiva kartāraṃ karaṇaṃ kriyām /
children.translated_text: You deny effect and cause, agent, instrument, and action,

children.text: utpādaṃ ca nirodhaṃ ca phalaṃ ca pratibādhase // MMK_24.17 //
children.translated_text: arising and cessation, and fruit.

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatāṃ tāṃ pracakṣmahe /
children.translated_text: That which is dependent co-arising—that we declare to be <s>śūnyatā</s>;

children.text: sā prajñaptir upādāya pratipat saiva madhyamā // MMK_24.18 //
children.translated_text: that is a dependent designation; that itself is the Middle Way.

children.text: apratītya samutpanno dharmaḥ kaścin na vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that has arisen without depending on something;

children.text: yasmāt tasmād aśūnyo hi dharmaḥ kaścin na vidyate // MMK_24.19 //
children.translated_text: therefore there is no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever that is non-empty.

children.text: yady aśūnyam idaṃ sarvam udayo nāsti na vyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all this were non-empty, there would be no arising and no passing away;

children.text: caturṇām āryasatyānām abhāvas te prasajyate // MMK_24.20 //
children.translated_text: it would follow for you that the four Noble Truths are non-existent.

children.text: apratītya samutpannaṃ kuto duḥkhaṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: How could suffering exist if not dependently arisen?

children.text: anityam uktaṃ duḥkhaṃ hi tat svābhāvye na vidyate // MMK_24.21 //
children.translated_text: Suffering has been declared to be impermanent; it does not exist in what has own-nature.

children.text: svabhāvato vidyamānaṃ kiṃ punaḥ samudeṣyate /
children.translated_text: That which exists by own-nature—how could it originate again?

children.text: tasmāt samudayo nāsti śūnyatāṃ pratibādhataḥ // MMK_24.22 //
children.translated_text: Therefore origination does not exist for one who denies <s>śūnyatā</s>.

children.text: na nirodhaḥ svabhāvena sato duḥkhasya vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is no cessation of suffering that exists by own-nature;

children.text: svabhāvaparyavasthānān nirodhaṃ pratibādhase // MMK_24.23 //
children.translated_text: by insisting on own-nature, you deny cessation.

children.text: svābhāvye sati mārgasya bhāvanā nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: If own-nature exists, the cultivation of the path is not possible;

children.text: athāsau bhāvyate mārgaḥ svābhāvyaṃ te na vidyate // MMK_24.24 //
children.translated_text: but if that path is cultivated, your own-nature does not exist.

children.text: yadā duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodhaś ca na vidyate /
children.translated_text: When suffering, origination, and cessation do not exist,

children.text: mārgo duḥkhanirodhatvāt katamaḥ prāpayiṣyati // MMK_24.25 //
children.translated_text: what path will lead to the cessation of suffering?

children.text: svabhāvenāparijñānaṃ yadi tasya punaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: If non-comprehension of suffering exists by own-nature, how then

children.text: parijñānaṃ nanu kila svabhāvaḥ samavasthitaḥ // MMK_24.26 //
children.translated_text: can there be comprehension of it? Does not own-nature remain fixed?

children.text: prahāṇasākṣātkaraṇe bhāvanā caivam eva te /
children.translated_text: Abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation likewise for you—

children.text: parijñāvan na yujyante catvāry api phalāni ca // MMK_24.27 //
children.translated_text: as with comprehension, are not coherent, nor are the four fruits.

children.text: svabhāvenānadhigataṃ yat phalaṃ tat punaḥ katham /
children.translated_text: A fruit not attained by own-nature—how then

children.text: śakyaṃ samadhigantuṃ syāt svabhāvaṃ parigṛhṇataḥ // MMK_24.28 //
children.translated_text: could it possibly be attained by one who grasps at own-nature?

children.text: phalābhāve phalasthā no na santi pratipannakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Without fruits, there are no attainers of fruits, nor those who have entered the path;

children.text: saṃgho nāsti na cet santi te 'ṣṭau puruṣapudgalāḥ // MMK_24.29 //
children.translated_text: if those eight types of persons do not exist, the <s>Saṃgha</s> does not exist.

children.text: abhāvāc cāryasatyānāṃ saddharmo 'pi na vidyate /
children.translated_text: From the non-existence of the Noble Truths, the true <s>Dharma</s> also does not exist;

children.text: dharme cāsati saṃghe ca kathaṃ buddho bhaviṣyati // MMK_24.30 //
children.translated_text: and if neither <s>Dharma</s> nor <s>Saṃgha</s> exist, how can there be a <s>Buddha</s>?

children.text: apratītyāpi bodhiṃ ca tava buddhaḥ prasajyate /
children.translated_text: For you, a <s>Buddha</s> would arise even without depending on <s>bodhi</s> (awakening);

children.text: apratītyāpi buddhaṃ ca tava bodhiḥ prasajyate // MMK_24.31 //
children.translated_text: for you, <s>bodhi</s> would arise even without depending on a <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: yaś cābuddhaḥ svabhāvena sa bodhāya ghaṭann api /
children.translated_text: One who by own-nature is not a <s>Buddha</s>, even striving for <s>bodhi</s>,

children.text: na bodhisattvacaryāyāṃ bodhiṃ te 'dhigamiṣyati // MMK_24.32 //
children.translated_text: will not attain <s>bodhi</s> in the practice of the <s>bodhisattva</s>.

children.text: na ca dharmam adharmaṃ vā kaścij jātu kariṣyati /
children.translated_text: And no one will ever perform <s>dharma</s> or <s>adharma</s>;

children.text: kim aṣūnyasya kartavyaṃ svabhāvaḥ kriyate na hi // MMK_24.33 //
children.translated_text: what is there to be done by the non-empty? Own-nature is not produced by action.

children.text: vinā dharmam adharmaṃ ca phalaṃ hi tava vidyate /
children.translated_text: For you, fruit exists apart from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>;

children.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ ca phalaṃ tava na vidyate // MMK_24.34 //
children.translated_text: and for you, fruit caused by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> does not exist.

children.text: dharmādharmanimittaṃ vā yadi te vidyate phalam /
children.translated_text: Or if for you fruit caused by <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> exists,

children.text: dharmādharmasamutpannam aśūnyaṃ te kathaṃ phalam // MMK_24.35 //
children.translated_text: how can fruit arisen from <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> be non-empty for you?

children.text: sarvasaṃvyvahārāṃś ca laukikān pratibādhase /
children.translated_text: You deny all worldly conventions

children.text: yat pratītyasamutpādaśūnyatāṃ pratibādhase // MMK_24.36 //
children.translated_text: in that you deny the <s>śūnyatā</s> of dependent co-arising.

children.text: na kartavyaṃ bhavet kiṃcid anārabdhā bhavet kriyā /
children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever would need to be done; action would be uncommenced;

children.text: kārakaḥ syād akurvāṇaḥ śūnyatāṃ pratibādhataḥ // MMK_24.37 //
children.translated_text: an agent would be one who does not act—for one who denies <s>śūnyatā</s>.

children.text: ajātam aniruddhaṃ ca kūṭaśthaṃ ca bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: Unborn, unceased, and immutable would the world be,

children.text: vicitrābhir avasthābhiḥ svabhāve rahitaṃ jagat // MMK_24.38 //
children.translated_text: devoid of its manifold states, if devoid of own-nature.

children.text: asaṃprāptasya ca prāptir duḥkhaparyantakarma ca /
children.translated_text: The attainment of the unattained, the making of an end to suffering,

children.text: sarvakleśaprahāṇaṃ ca yady aśūnyaṃ na vidyate // MMK_24.39 //
children.translated_text: and the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)—if non-empty, these do not exist.

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaṃ paśyatīdaṃ sa paśyati /
children.translated_text: One who sees dependent co-arising sees this:

children.text: duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ caiva nirodhaṃ mārgam eva ca // MMK_24.40 //
children.translated_text: suffering, origination, cessation, and the path.

children.text: yadi śūnyam idaṃ sarvam udayo nāsti na vyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all this is empty, there is no arising and no passing away;

children.text: prahāṇād vā nirodhād vā kasya nirvāṇam iṣyate // MMK_25.1 //
children.translated_text: by whose abandonment or cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s> sought?

children.text: yady aśūnyam idaṃ sarvam udayo nāsti na vyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If all this is non-empty, there is no arising and no passing away;

children.text: prahāṇād vā nirodhād vā kasya nirvāṇam iṣyate // MMK_25.2 //
children.translated_text: by whose abandonment or cessation is <s>nirvāṇa</s> sought?

children.text: aprahīṇam asaṃprāptam anucchinnam aśāśvatam /
children.translated_text: Not abandoned and not attained, not annihilated and not eternal,

children.text: aniruddham anutpannam etan nirvāṇam ucyate // MMK_25.3 //
children.translated_text: not ceased and not arisen—this is called <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: bhāvas tāvan na nirvāṇaṃ jarāmaraṇalakṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: First of all, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not a positive entity, for it would have the marks of aging and death;

children.text: prasajyetāsti bhāvo hi na jarāmaraṇaṃ vinā // MMK_25.4 //
children.translated_text: for there is no positive entity without aging and death.

children.text: bhāvaś ca yadi nirvāṇaṃ nirvāṇaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> were a positive entity, <s>nirvāṇa</s> would be conditioned;

children.text: nāsaṃskṛto hi vidyate bhāvaḥ kva cana kaś cana // MMK_25.5 //
children.translated_text: for no positive entity whatsoever is found anywhere that is unconditioned.

children.text: bhāvaś ca yadi nirvāṇam anupādāya tat katham /
children.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> were a positive entity, how could it be without clinging?

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ nānupādāya kaścid bhāvo hi vidyate // MMK_25.6 //
children.translated_text: For no positive entity whatsoever is found without clinging.

children.text: bhāvo yadi na nirvāṇam abhāvaḥ kiṃ bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not a positive entity, could it then be a negative entity?

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ yatra bhāvo na nābhāvas tatra vidyate // MMK_25.7 //
children.translated_text: Where there is no positive entity, there is no negative entity either.

children.text: yady abhāvaś ca nirvāṇam anupādāya tat katham /
children.translated_text: And if <s>nirvāṇa</s> were a negative entity, how could it be without clinging?

children.text: nirvāṇaṃ na hy abhāvo 'sti yo 'nupādāya vidyate // MMK_25.8 //
children.translated_text: For no negative entity is found that exists without clinging.

children.text: ya ājavaṃjavībhāva upādāya pratītya vā /
children.translated_text: That which is the process of coming and going, dependent and conditioned—

children.text: so 'pratītyānupādāya nirvāṇam upadiśyate // MMK_25.9 //
children.translated_text: that, without dependence and without clinging, is taught to be <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

children.text: prahāṇaṃ cābravīc chāstā bhavasya vibhavasya ca /
children.translated_text: The Teacher taught the abandonment of both existence and non-existence;

children.text: tasmān na bhāvo nābhāvo nirvāṇam iti yujyate // MMK_25.10 //
children.translated_text: therefore it is fitting that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither being nor non-being.

children.text: bhaved abhāvo bhāvaś ca nirvāṇam ubhayaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were both being and non-being,

children.text: bhaved abhāvo bhāvaś ca mokṣas tac ca na yujyate // MMK_25.11 //
children.translated_text: then liberation would be both being and non-being—and that is not coherent.

children.text: bhaved abhāvo bhāvaś ca nirvāṇam ubhayaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> were both being and non-being,

children.text: nānupādāya nirvāṇam upādāyobhayaṃ hi tat // MMK_25.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>nirvāṇa</s> would not be without clinging, for both involve clinging.

children.text: bhaved abhāvo bhāvaś ca nirvāṇam ubhayaṃ katham /
children.translated_text: How could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be both being and non-being?

children.text: asaṃskṛtaṃ hi nirvāṇaṃ bhāvābhāvau ca saṃskṛtau // MMK_25.13 //
children.translated_text: For <s>nirvāṇa</s> is unconditioned, while being and non-being are conditioned.

children.text: bhaved abhāvo bhāvaś ca nirvāṇa ubhayaṃ katham /
children.translated_text: How could <s>nirvāṇa</s> be both being and non-being?

children.text: tayor abhāvo hy ekatra prakāśatamasor iva // MMK_25.14 //
children.translated_text: For the two cannot co-exist in one place, like light and darkness.

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāvo nirvāṇam iti yā 'ñjanā /
children.translated_text: The assertion that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is neither non-being nor being—

children.text: abhāve caiva bhāve ca sā siddhe sati sidhyati // MMK_25.15 //
children.translated_text: that would be established only if non-being and being were established.

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāvo nirvāṇaṃ yadi vidyate /
children.translated_text: If <s>nirvāṇa</s> is found to be neither non-being nor being,

children.text: naivābhāvo naiva bhāva iti kena tad ajyate // MMK_25.16 //
children.translated_text: by whom is it asserted to be 'neither non-being nor being'?

children.text: paraṃ nirodhād bhagavān bhavatīty eva nājyate /
children.translated_text: It is not asserted that the Blessed One exists after cessation,

children.text: na bhavaty ubhayaṃ ceti nobhayaṃ ceti nājyate // MMK_25.17 //
children.translated_text: nor that he does not exist, nor both, nor neither.

children.text: tiṣṭhamāno 'pi bhagavān bhavatīty eva nājyate /
children.translated_text: Even while living, it is not asserted that the Blessed One exists,

children.text: na bhavaty ubhayaṃ ceti nobhayaṃ ceti nājyate // MMK_25.18 //
children.translated_text: nor that he does not exist, nor both, nor neither.

children.text: na saṃsārasya nirvāṇāt kiṃcid asti viśeṣaṇam /
children.translated_text: There is not the slightest difference between <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>;

children.text: na nirvāṇasya saṃsārāt kiṃcid asti viśeṣaṇam // MMK_25.19 //
children.translated_text: there is not the slightest difference between <s>nirvāṇa</s> and <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: nirvāṇasya ca yā koṭiḥ koṭiḥ saṃsaraṇasya ca /
children.translated_text: The limit of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is the limit of <s>saṃsāra</s>;

children.text: na tayor antaraṃ kiṃcit susūkṣmam api vidyate // MMK_25.20 //
children.translated_text: between the two, not even the subtlest distinction is found.

children.text: paraṃ nirodhād antādyāḥ śāśvatādyāś ca dṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Views about what is after cessation—whether finite, eternal, and the like—

children.text: nirvāṇam aparāntaṃ ca pūrvāntaṃ ca samāśritāḥ // MMK_25.21 //
children.translated_text: are dependent upon <s>nirvāṇa</s> as a posterior limit and an anterior limit.

children.text: śūnyeṣu sarvadharmeṣu kim anantaṃ kim antavat /
children.translated_text: When all <s>dharmas</s> are empty, what is infinite? What is finite?

children.text: kim anantam antavac ca nānantaṃ nāntavac ca kim // MMK_25.22 //
children.translated_text: What is both infinite and finite? What is neither infinite nor finite?

children.text: kiṃ tad eva kim anyat kiṃ śāśvataṃ kim aśāśvatam /
children.translated_text: What is identical? What is different? What is eternal? What is non-eternal?

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca kiṃ vā nobhayam apy atha // MMK_25.23 //
children.translated_text: What is both eternal and non-eternal? What is neither?

children.text: sarvopalambhopaśamaḥ prapañcopaśamaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: The quiescence of all apprehension, the quiescence of <s>prapañca</s> (conceptual proliferation)—that is bliss;

children.text: na kva cit kasyacit kaścid dharmo buddhena deśitaḥ // MMK_25.24 //
children.translated_text: no <s>dharma</s> whatsoever was taught by the <s>Buddha</s> to anyone anywhere.

children.text: punarbhavāya saṃskārān avidyānivṛtas tridhā /
children.translated_text: Enveloped by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), one constructs the threefold

children.text: abhisaṃskurute yāṃs tair gatiṃ gacchati karmabhiḥ // MMK_26.1 //
children.translated_text: <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations) for renewed existence, and by those actions goes to a destiny.

children.text: vijñānaṃ saṃniviśate saṃskārapratyayaṃ gatau /
children.translated_text: Consciousness, conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s>, enters a destiny;

children.text: saṃniviṣṭe 'tha vijñāne nāmarūpaṃ niṣicyate // MMK_26.2 //
children.translated_text: when consciousness has entered, <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form) is infused.

children.text: niṣikte nāmarūpe tu ṣaḍāyatanasaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>nāmarūpa</s> has been infused, the six sense-bases (<s>ṣaḍāyatana</s>) arise;

children.text: ṣaḍāyatanam āgamya saṃsparśaḥ saṃpravartate // MMK_26.3 //
children.translated_text: with the arising of the six sense-bases, contact (<s>sparśa</s>) proceeds.

children.text: cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpaṃ ca samanvāhāram eva ca /
children.translated_text: Dependent on the eye and form, and on attention,

children.text: nāmarūpaṃ pratītyaivaṃ vijñānaṃ saṃpravartate // MMK_26.4 //
children.translated_text: dependent on <s>nāmarūpa</s>, consciousness thus proceeds.

children.text: saṃnipātas trayāṇāṃ yo rūpavijñānacakṣuṣām /
children.translated_text: The conjunction of the three—form, consciousness, and the eye—

children.text: sparśaḥ sa tasmāt sparśāc ca vedanā saṃpravartate // MMK_26.5 //
children.translated_text: that is contact; from contact, feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) proceeds.

children.text: vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā vedanārthaṃ hi tṛṣyate /
children.translated_text: Conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>); one craves for the objects of feeling;

children.text: tṛṣyamāṇa upādānam upādatte caturvidham // MMK_26.6 //
children.translated_text: while craving, one takes up the fourfold clinging (<s>upādāna</s>).

children.text: upādāne sati bhava upādātuḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: When there is clinging, the existence (<s>bhava</s>) of the one who clings proceeds;

children.text: syād dhi yady anupādāno mucyeta na bhaved bhavaḥ // MMK_26.7 //
children.translated_text: for if one were without clinging, one would be liberated—there would be no existence.

children.text: pañca skandhāḥ sa ca bhavo bhavāj jātiḥ pravartate /
children.translated_text: That existence is the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates); from existence, birth proceeds;

children.text: jarāmaraṇaduḥkhādi śokāḥ saparidevanāḥ // MMK_26.8 //
children.translated_text: aging, death, suffering, and the like—grief with lamentation,

children.text: daurmanasyam upāyāsā jāter etat pravartate /
children.translated_text: distress and anguish—proceed from birth;

children.text: kevalasyaivam etasya duḥkhaskandhasya saṃbhavaḥ // MMK_26.9 //
children.translated_text: thus arises this entire mass of suffering alone.

children.text: saṃsāramūlaṃ saṃskārān avidvān saṃskaroty ataḥ /
children.translated_text: The root of <s>saṃsāra</s> is the <s>saṃskāras</s>; therefore the ignorant one constructs them;

children.text: avidvān kārakas tasmān na vidvāṃs tattvadarśanāt // MMK_26.10 //
children.translated_text: the ignorant one is the agent, but not the wise one, due to seeing reality.

children.text: avidyāyāṃ niruddhāyāṃ saṃskārāṇām asaṃbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>avidyā</s> has ceased, the <s>saṃskāras</s> do not arise;

children.text: avidyāyā nirodhas tu jñānasyāsyaiva bhāvanāt // MMK_26.11 //
children.translated_text: the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> comes through the cultivation of this very knowledge.

children.text: tasya tasya nirodhena tat tan nābhipravartate /
children.translated_text: Through the cessation of each link, each successive link does not proceed;

children.text: duḥkhaskandhaḥ kevalo 'yam evaṃ samyag nirudhyate // MMK_26.12 //
children.translated_text: this entire mass of suffering alone is thus rightly ceased.

children.text: abhūm atītam adhvānaṃ nābhūvam iti dṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Views such as 'I existed in a past period' or 'I did not exist'—

children.text: yās tāḥ śāśvatalokādyāḥ pūrvāntaṃ samupāśritāḥ // MMK_27.1 //
children.translated_text: those views such as 'the world is eternal' and the rest, which are dependent on the prior limit— (MMK 27.1)

children.text: dṛṣṭayo na bhaviṣyāmi kim anyo 'nāgate 'dhvani /
children.translated_text: the views 'I shall not exist'—what? 'another'?—in the future course of time,

children.text: bhaviṣyāmīti cāntādyā aparāntaṃ samāśritāḥ // MMK_27.2 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall exist' and so forth, which are dependent on the posterior limit— (MMK 27.2)

children.text: abhūm atītam adhvānam ity etan nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: 'I existed in the past course of time'—this is not tenable,

children.text: yo hi janmasu pūrveṣu sa eva na bhavaty ayam // MMK_27.3 //
children.translated_text: for the one who existed in previous births is not this very same one. (MMK 27.3)

children.text: sa evātmeti tu bhaved upādānaṃ viśiṣyate /
children.translated_text: If it were the very same self, then <s>upādāna</s> (appropriation) would have to be distinguished;

children.text: upādānavinirmukta ātmā te katamaḥ punaḥ // MMK_27.4 //
children.translated_text: but apart from appropriation, what then is your self? (MMK 27.4)

children.text: upādānavinirmukto nāsty ātmeti kṛte sati /
children.translated_text: If it is granted that there is no self apart from appropriation,

children.text: syād upādānam evātmā nāsti cātmeti vaḥ punaḥ // MMK_27.5 //
children.translated_text: then appropriation itself would be the self—but then for you there is no self. (MMK 27.5)

children.text: na copādānam evātmā vyeti tat samudeti ca /
children.translated_text: Nor is appropriation itself the self, for it perishes and arises;

children.text: kathaṃ hi nāmopādānam upādātā bhaviṣyati // MMK_27.6 //
children.translated_text: how indeed can appropriation become the appropriator? (MMK 27.6)

children.text: anyaḥ punar upādānād ātmā naivopapadyate /
children.translated_text: A self that is other than appropriation is simply not tenable;

children.text: gṛhyeta hy anupādāno yady anyo na ca gṛhyate // MMK_27.7 //
children.translated_text: if it were other, it would be apprehended without appropriation—yet it is not so apprehended. (MMK 27.7)

children.text: evaṃ nānya upādānān na copādānam eva saḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the self is neither other than appropriation, nor is it appropriation itself;

children.text: ātmā nāsty anupādāno nāpi nāsty eṣa niścayaḥ // MMK_27.8 //
children.translated_text: there is no self without appropriation—yet it is also not the case that it does not exist; this is the ascertainment. (MMK 27.8)

children.text: nābhūm atītam adhvānam ity etan nopapadyate /
children.translated_text: 'I did not exist in the past course of time'—this is not tenable,

children.text: yo hi janmasu pūrveṣu tato 'nyo na bhavaty ayam // MMK_27.9 //
children.translated_text: for the one who existed in previous births is not other than this one. (MMK 27.9)

children.text: yadi hy ayaṃ bhaved anyaḥ pratyākhyāyāpi taṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If this one were other, he would exist even having rejected that one;

children.text: tathaiva ca sa saṃtiṣṭhet tatra jāyeta cāmṛtaḥ // MMK_27.10 //
children.translated_text: likewise that one would persist, and one would be born here as immortal. (MMK 27.10)

children.text: ucchedaḥ karmaṇāṃ nāśaḥ kṛtam anyena karma ca /
children.translated_text: Annihilation, destruction of <s>karma</s> (action), and the experiencing by one of the <s>karma</s> done by another—

children.text: pratisaṃvedayed anya evam ādi prasajyate // MMK_27.11 //
children.translated_text: these and other [absurdities] would follow. (MMK 27.11)

children.text: nāpy abhūtvā samudbhūto doṣo hy atra prasajyate /
children.translated_text: Nor is it tenable that [the self], not having existed, came into being, for a fault follows here:

children.text: kṛtako vā bhaved ātmā saṃbhūto vāpy ahetukaḥ // MMK_27.12 //
children.translated_text: the self would either be fabricated, or would have arisen without a cause. (MMK 27.12)

children.text: evaṃ dṛṣtir atīte yā nābhūm aham abhūm aham /
children.translated_text: Thus, the views concerning the past—'I existed,' 'I did not exist,'

children.text: ubhayaṃ nobhayaṃ ceti naiṣā samupapadyate // MMK_27.13 //
children.translated_text: 'both,' and 'neither'—none of these are tenable. (MMK 27.13)

children.text: adhvany anāgate kiṃ nu bhaviṣyāmīti darśanam /
children.translated_text: In the future course of time, the views 'shall I exist?'

children.text: na bhaviṣyāmi cety etad atītenādhvanā samam // MMK_27.14 //
children.translated_text: and 'shall I not exist?' are equivalent to those regarding the past course of time. (MMK 27.14)

children.text: sa devaḥ sa manuṣyaś ced evaṃ bhavati śāśvatam /
children.translated_text: If the god is the same as the human being, then it would be eternal;

children.text: anutpannaś ca devaḥ syāj jāyate na hi śāśvatam // MMK_27.15 //
children.translated_text: and the god would be unborn—for the eternal is not born. (MMK 27.15)

children.text: devād anyo manuṣyaś ced aśāśvatam ato bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the human being is other than the god, it would be non-eternal;

children.text: devād anyo manuṣyaś cet saṃtatir nopapadyate // MMK_27.16 //
children.translated_text: and if the human being is other than the god, continuity is not tenable. (MMK 27.16)

children.text: divyo yady ekadeśaḥ syād ekdeśaś ca mānuṣaḥ /
children.translated_text: If one part were divine and another part human,

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca bhavet tac ca na yujyate // MMK_27.17 //
children.translated_text: it would be both non-eternal and eternal—and that is not tenable. (MMK 27.17)

children.text: aśāśvataṃ śāśvataṃ ca prasiddham ubhayaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If both the non-eternal and the eternal were established,

children.text: siddhe na śāśvataṃ kāmaṃ naivāśāśvatam ity api // MMK_27.18 //
children.translated_text: then surely neither 'eternal' alone nor 'non-eternal' alone would be established either. (MMK 27.18)

children.text: kutaścid āgataḥ kaścit kiṃcid gacchet punaḥ kva cit /
children.translated_text: If someone came from somewhere and went to somewhere else,

children.text: yadi tasmād anādis tu saṃsāraḥ syān na cāsti saḥ // MMK_27.19 //
children.translated_text: then <s>saṃsāra</s> would be beginningless—but that [person] does not exist. (MMK 27.19)

children.text: nāsti cec chāśvataḥ kaścit ko bhaviṣyaty aśāśvataḥ /
children.translated_text: If there is no one who is eternal, who will be non-eternal?

children.text: śāśvato 'śāśvataś cāpi dvābhyām ābhyāṃ tiraskṛtaḥ // MMK_27.20 //
children.translated_text: And the one who is both eternal and non-eternal is excluded by both these [refutations]. (MMK 27.20)

children.text: antavān yadi lokaḥ syāt paralokaḥ kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: If the world were finite, how could there be another world?

children.text: athāpy anantavāl lokaḥ paralokaḥ kathaṃ bhavet // MMK_27.21 //
children.translated_text: And if the world were infinite, how could there be another world? (MMK 27.21)

children.text: skandhānām eṣa saṃtāno yasmād dīpārciṣām iva /
children.translated_text: Since the continuity of the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) is like that of a series of lamp-flames,

children.text: tasmān nānantavattvaṃ ca nāntavattvaṃ ca yujyate // MMK_27.22 //
children.translated_text: therefore neither infinitude nor finitude is tenable. (MMK 27.22)

children.text: pūrve yadi ca bhajyerann utpadyeran na cāpy amī /
children.translated_text: If the prior [aggregates] were to perish and these [present] aggregates were not to arise

children.text: skandhāḥ skandhān pratītyemān atha loko 'ntavān bhavet // MMK_27.23 //
children.translated_text: dependent on those aggregates, then the world would be finite. (MMK 27.23)

children.text: pūrve yadi na bhajyerann utpadyeran na cāpyamī /
children.translated_text: If the prior [aggregates] were not to perish and these [present] aggregates were not to arise

children.text: skandhāḥ skandhān pratītyemāl loko 'nanto bhaved atha // MMK_27.24 //
children.translated_text: dependent on those aggregates, then the world would be infinite. (MMK 27.24)

children.text: antavān ekadeśaś ced ekadeśas tv anantavān /
children.translated_text: If one part were finite and another part were infinite,

children.text: syād antavān anantaś ca lokas tac ca na yujyate // MMK_27.25 //
children.translated_text: the world would be both finite and infinite—and that is not tenable. (MMK 27.25)

children.text: kathaṃ tāvad upādātur ekadeśo vinaṅkṣyate /
children.translated_text: How indeed could one part of the appropriator perish

children.text: na naṅkṣyate caikadeśa evaṃ caitan na yujyate // MMK_27.26 //
children.translated_text: while another part does not perish? This too is not tenable. (MMK 27.26)

children.text: upādānaikadeśaś ca kathaṃ nāma vinaṅkṣyate /
children.translated_text: And how could one part of appropriation perish

children.text: na naṅkṣyate caikadeśo naitad apy upapadyate // MMK_27.27 //
children.translated_text: while another part does not perish? This too is not tenable. (MMK 27.27)

children.text: antavac cāpy anantaṃ ca prasiddham ubhayaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If both 'finite' and 'infinite' were established,

children.text: siddhe naivāntavat kāmaṃ naivānantavad ity api // MMK_27.28 //
children.translated_text: then surely neither 'finite' alone nor 'infinite' alone would be established either. (MMK 27.28)

children.text: atha vā sarvabhāvānāṃ śūnyatvāc chāśvatādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, since all entities are empty, where, of whom, which,

children.text: kva kasya katamāḥ kasmāt saṃbhaviṣyanti dṛṣṭayaḥ // MMK_27.29 //
children.translated_text: and from what will the views of eternalism and the rest arise? (MMK 27.29)

children.text: sarvadṛṣṭiprahāṇāya yaḥ saddharmam adeśayat /
children.translated_text: To him who, out of compassion,

children.text: anukampām upādāya taṃ namasyāmi gautamam // MMK_27.30 //
children.translated_text: taught the true <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of all views—to that <s>Gautama</s> I pay homage. (MMK 27.30)
